The seven-tier black soldier fly larval bioconversion system demonstrates the larvae’s growth process, with newly hatched larvae introduced at the top tier and gradually moving through each level as they consume organic food waste and mature. (Photo by IMES)

After reaching maturity, the black soldier fly larvae are automatically sorted by size using a screening machine before being processed into protein-rich animal feed, while the remaining organic residue is converted into fertilizer. (Photo by IMES)

			Date :
			 2026-07-21 

			Department : 
			International Master’s Program of Applied Economics and Social Development

【Article by IMES 】

Students from the International Master's in Applied Economics and Social Development (IMES) program at National Chengchi University (NCCU) recently toured an off-site food waste processing facility operated by a local hotpot restaurant chain that has adopted a black soldier fly larval bioconversion system. The visit, organized by IMES Professor Alicia Say, gave students a firsthand look at how food waste from a restaurant is transformed into animal feed and organic fertilizer.

The facility is where Professor Cheng-Jen Shih of National Taiwan University has deployed his patented bioconversion system, which pioneers the use of black soldier fly larvae for food waste conversion and circular resource utilization in Taiwan. Through partnerships with local businesses, Professor Shih has demonstrated how academic research can be translated into practical waste management solutions, including this facility, where the restaurant's food waste is processed through larval bioconversion.

During the tour, students observed the full waste-to-resource pipeline, from raw food waste intake to larval processing and end-product extraction. They observed different stages of larval cultivation, learned about feedstock preparation and environmental controls, and discussed the operational and economic considerations of scaling insect-based waste treatment. Professor Shih also noted that the entire operation is a closed-loop, low-risk process requiring only a single worker to run, even though the machine itself can handle up to 300 kg of food waste.

This scalability point carried into the broader significance of the visit: insect-based bioconversion represents a viable alternative to conventional food waste disposal methods while simultaneously generating economic value through protein-rich biomass. The conversation also turned to the policy context surrounding food waste management in Taiwan. The experience comes at a timely moment, as Taiwan moves toward a ban on feeding food waste to livestock by the end of 2026, prompting restaurants and companies across the country to seek sustainable alternatives for organic waste management.

"What struck me most was how scalable this model could be. A single machine handling this much waste with minimal labor makes me think about what it could mean for large commercial complexes looking for solutions for their own food waste footprint," said Ha Do, an IMES student from Vietnam.

This experience offered students a direct window into how academic research in sustainable waste management translates into scalable, real-world application. It bridges classroom concepts such as social innovation and sustainability into active industry practice. The site visit reflects IMES's commitment to connecting academic knowledge with practical engagement. By exposing students to emerging sustainability innovations and industry collaboration, the program aims to cultivate future professionals capable of addressing complex environmental and social challenges through interdisciplinary thinking and applied research.

 TAIPEI, July 8, 2026

			Date :
			 2026-07-20 

			Department : 
			Office of International Cooperation (OIC)

【Article by OIC】

Funded by Ministry of Education, Prof. Chien-Wu Hsueh, Section Chief of the Mainland Affairs Section, along with Senior Regional Manager Ms. Kelly Wang, at the Office of International Cooperation (OIC), National Chengchi University (NCCU) recently led a group of 14 well-selected NCCU students to attend 2026 International Summer Semester at Sungkyunkwan University (SKKU) in Seoul, South Korea, as part of its ongoing internationalization and bilingual education initiatives. During this month-long summer program, NCCU students can freely select three courses based on their academic interests from fields like Business & Economy, Social Sciences & Humanities, Computer & Data Science, Engineering, to Korean Language Studies. The courses were taught not only by faculty from SKKU but also by guest professors from renowned international institutions such as the University of South Carolina and Michigan State University, etc.

The initiative highlights the long-standing relationship between NCCU and SKKU, which dates back to 1964 when the two institutions signed their first academic cooperation agreement, making each other mutually their very first partnership in the world. Today, SKKU is ranked 126th globally in the 2026 QS World University Rankings, receives substantial investment from the Samsung Group, and remains one of the top five universities for corporate recruitment in South Korea. 

During this trip, Prof. Hsueh and the student group also visited the Taipei Mission in Korea and met with the Director of the Education Division Cheng-Kie Cheng, Secretary Jing-Yi Wong, and Ms. Cheng Han-Fei. The discussion focused on the current status of educational exchange activities between Taiwan and South Korea, as well as English-Medium Instruction (EMI) policies. Director Cheng noted that while the South Korean government actively promotes English education through initiatives like "English Villages," its universities face challenges similar to Taiwan regarding a shortage of qualified EMI faculty. He also shared observations on the competitive nature of early-childhood English education in South Korea, where children as young as 4 years old sometimes need to take competitive entrance examinations to enter private English immersion kindergartens.

In addition to the summer program activities at SKKU, the OIC representatives also visited several other partners in Seoul, including Hanyang University, Seoul National University, and Korea University to discuss ways to strengthen collaborations. At SKKU, discussions focused on faculty exchange mechanism and expanding future cooperation in summer programs. At Hanyang University, the two sides discussed the possibility of co-hosting future summer modules in Taiwan, drawing on Hanyang's previous experience with Japanese and domestic universities. At Seoul National University, both parties expressed a mutual desire to actively encourage joint research projects while at Korea University, the discussion circulate around reviewing incentives to encourage more Korea University students to study in Taiwan, and exploring opportunities for faculty exchange.

Before concluding the trip, the OIC representatives met with NCCU exchange and degree-seeking students currently studying at Yonsei University, Dongguk University, and the University of Seoul to learn about their academic progress and future career plans. The OIC stated that the university will continue to coordinate international resources to provide further learning and research opportunities for NCCU faculty and students.

			Date :
			 2026-07-16 

			Department : 
			Master’s Program in Global Communication and Innovation Technology

【Article by GCIT】

Professor Edson C. Tandoc Jr. of Nanyang Technological University (NTU), Singapore, made a return visit to the Master’s program in Global Communication and Innovation Technology (GCIT) from July 8 to 25, 2026, to teach a three-week, English-taught summer intensive course titled “AI, Media, and Information Integrity.” The course examines the interplay between artificial intelligence and the contemporary media environment, guiding students to explore how AI is transforming the production, dissemination, and reception of information, as well as the challenges it poses to media trust, information integrity, and democratic societies.

Professor Tandoc is a faculty member at NTU’s Wee Kim Wee School of Communication and Information (WKWSCI). He also serves as the school’s Associate Chair for Research and Director of the Center for Information Integrity and the Internet (IN-Cube). His research focuses on journalism and communication, misinformation and disinformation, digital platforms, and the impact of artificial intelligence on the media industry and the public information environment. Following his visit to GCIT in 2025, during which he conducted a workshop and delivered a public lecture, Professor Tandoc returned this year to further strengthen academic exchange between the two institutions in the areas of AI, media, and information integrity.

The course covers a broad range of topics, including the history and theoretical foundations of AI, media ecology, applications of AI in journalism and advertising, the creative industries, deepfakes and misinformation, and AI and mental health. It attracted students from GCIT as well as the departments of psychology, radio and television, and Chinese literature, along with international students. Their diverse academic and cultural backgrounds enriched classroom discussions and fostered interdisciplinary and cross-cultural exchange.

In addition to Professor Tandoc, several scholars from NTU’s Wee Kim Wee School of Communication and Information contributed guest lectures to the course. Associate Professor Chen Lou and Assistant Professor Andrew Prahl discussed the applications of generative AI in public relations and advertising, as well as consumer perceptions of AI-generated content. Assistant Professor Pei-Sze Chow examined how generative AI is transforming practices in the creative industries. Associate Professor Saifuddin Ahmed focused on deepfakes, misinformation governance, and the current development of AI. Nanyang Assistant Professor Renwen Zhang explored human–AI interaction, algorithmic risks, and the potential effects of AI on mental health. Drawing on their respective areas of expertise, the guest speakers helped students develop a more comprehensive understanding of the opportunities and challenges AI presents for media and society.

Professor Tammy Lin, Director of GCIT, emphasized that as AI continues to reshape global communication and media, the program remains committed to cultivating students’ international perspectives, interdisciplinary capabilities, and critical thinking skills. Professor Tandoc’s visit and the NTU faculty team’s online lectures strengthened international academic collaboration while providing students with access to the latest research and industry insights.

After reaching maturity, the black soldier fly larvae are automatically sorted by size using a screening machine before being processed into protein-rich animal feed, while the remaining organic residue is converted into fertilizer. (Photo by IMES)

			Date :
			 2026-07-21 

			Department : 
			International Master’s Program of Applied Economics and Social Development

【Article by IMES 】

Students from the International Master's in Applied Economics and Social Development (IMES) program at National Chengchi University (NCCU) recently toured an off-site food waste processing facility operated by a local hotpot restaurant chain that has adopted a black soldier fly larval bioconversion system. The visit, organized by IMES Professor Alicia Say, gave students a firsthand look at how food waste from a restaurant is transformed into animal feed and organic fertilizer.

The facility is where Professor Cheng-Jen Shih of National Taiwan University has deployed his patented bioconversion system, which pioneers the use of black soldier fly larvae for food waste conversion and circular resource utilization in Taiwan. Through partnerships with local businesses, Professor Shih has demonstrated how academic research can be translated into practical waste management solutions, including this facility, where the restaurant's food waste is processed through larval bioconversion.

During the tour, students observed the full waste-to-resource pipeline, from raw food waste intake to larval processing and end-product extraction. They observed different stages of larval cultivation, learned about feedstock preparation and environmental controls, and discussed the operational and economic considerations of scaling insect-based waste treatment. Professor Shih also noted that the entire operation is a closed-loop, low-risk process requiring only a single worker to run, even though the machine itself can handle up to 300 kg of food waste.

This scalability point carried into the broader significance of the visit: insect-based bioconversion represents a viable alternative to conventional food waste disposal methods while simultaneously generating economic value through protein-rich biomass. The conversation also turned to the policy context surrounding food waste management in Taiwan. The experience comes at a timely moment, as Taiwan moves toward a ban on feeding food waste to livestock by the end of 2026, prompting restaurants and companies across the country to seek sustainable alternatives for organic waste management.

"What struck me most was how scalable this model could be. A single machine handling this much waste with minimal labor makes me think about what it could mean for large commercial complexes looking for solutions for their own food waste footprint," said Ha Do, an IMES student from Vietnam.

This experience offered students a direct window into how academic research in sustainable waste management translates into scalable, real-world application. It bridges classroom concepts such as social innovation and sustainability into active industry practice. The site visit reflects IMES's commitment to connecting academic knowledge with practical engagement. By exposing students to emerging sustainability innovations and industry collaboration, the program aims to cultivate future professionals capable of addressing complex environmental and social challenges through interdisciplinary thinking and applied research.

 TAIPEI, July 8, 2026

			Date :
			 2026-07-16 

			Department : 
			Office of Fellowships for Austronesian Studies

【Article by Office of Fellowships for Austronesian Studies 】

The second session of the 2026 Austronesian Studies Lecture Series, organized by the Office of Fellowships for Austronesian Studies at National Chengchi University (NCCU), was held on May 26. The event was hosted by Professor Da-Wei Kuan, Chair of the Department of Ethnology and Convener of the Austronesian Research Center. He gave a brief introduction to the event and welcomed Professor Emerita Barbara Watson Andaya, one of the world's leading scholars of Southeast Asian history. Professor Andaya is Professor of Asian Studies at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa and former Director of its Center for Southeast Asian Studies. She has made significant contributions to the study of Maritime Southeast Asia.

Professor Kuan then invited Dean Wan-Ying Yang of the College of Social Sciences to deliver the opening remarks. Dean Yang noted that NCCU's Department of Ethnology, the first and only department of its kind in Taiwan, has long promoted interdisciplinary research on peoples, cultures, history, geography, and ethnic relations. She added that Professor Andaya's visit reflected the department's commitment to interdisciplinary dialogue. Dean Yang also noted that her own research on gender politics shares common ground with Professor Andaya's scholarship on gender.

Following the opening remarks, Professor Andaya delivered her lecture, emphasizing that gender should not be treated as a secondary topic in history but as a central dimension of human experience.

She noted that although gender studies only emerged as an academic field in the second half of the 20th century during the female liberation in the United States, questions surrounding gender roles, identity, and social relationships have always shaped the ways societies function and remember themselves.

One of the lecture’s central themes was the idea of “deep history,” which seeks to expand historical inquiry beyond written documentation by drawing on archaeology, genetics, paleoanthropology, linguistics, and environmental evidence. Professor Andaya argued that island Southeast Asia has often been overlooked in discussions of deep history compared to mainland Southeast Asia, largely because archaeological research in the region developed later. However, recent discoveries across the Malay Archipelago have increasingly challenged this assumption and opened new possibilities for understanding the distant human past.

Using examples from Java, Sulawesi, Borneo, the Philippines, and eastern Indonesia, Professor Andaya demonstrated how material culture can reveal complex understandings of gender and spirituality. She discussed prehistoric cave paintings of pigs found in Sulawesi, explaining that animals in many maritime Southeast Asian societies were not simply part of the natural environment, but were deeply connected to ritual practices, cosmology, and ancestor worship. 

The lecture also introduced several important archaeological discoveries, including human remains from Niah Cave in Sarawak, the Homo Floresiensis (Flores Man) findings on Flores Island, and the female burial known as Bessé was discovered in Sulawesi. Through burial analysis and DNA research, scholars have begun to reconsider assumptions about the important roles women may have played in early societies, including hunting, fishing, and ritual activities. Professor Andaya pointed out that archaeology has long tended to interpret early societies through a male-centered lens, but newer approaches increasingly challenge these earlier assumptions and encourage more nuanced readings of the past.

Beyond archaeology, Professor Andaya examined textiles, weapons, and ritual objects as important forms of historical evidence. In many Southeast Asian societies, weaving was traditionally associated with women, yet textiles themselves carried meanings related to ancestry, prestige, and social authority. She also discussed the Kris (Keris in Malay) dagger in the Malay world, describing how its blade and sheath symbolically represented masculine and feminine forces. By reading objects not merely as artifacts but as cultural expressions, she argued, historians are able to reconstruct deeper understandings of gender, power, and belief in maritime Southeast Asia.

The lecture was followed by a discussion session featuring Professor Courtney Work and Professor Yayut Yi‑Shiuan Chen from the Department of Ethnology at NCCU. Reflecting on Professor Andaya’s presentation, Professor Work highlighted the importance of challenging rigid boundaries and categories in historical interpretation. Drawing on examples such as pigs and tigers in Southeast Asian ritual traditions, she noted that animals in many Austronesian societies occupy symbolic and spiritual roles that cannot easily be understood through modern scientific classifications alone.

Professor Yayut responded by connecting the lecture to her fieldwork in Palau. Using the example of taro cultivation, she noted that although changing labor patterns may suggest a decline in women's roles, ethnographic research shows that women continue to hold significant authority in Palauan society. She emphasized that researchers should avoid imposing modern assumptions about gender and labor on local societies. 

Audience members also raised questions concerning colonialism, religion, and language politics. Concluding the lecture, Professor Andaya remarked that many questions surrounding gender and deep history remain unresolved, but this kind of  uncertainty is precisely what keeps Southeast Asian studies intellectually dynamic. She emphasized that future research will increasingly rely on collaboration across disciplines, particularly between historians, anthropologists, archaeologists, and linguists, in order to better understand the complexity of human societies across time.

Department of Turkish Language and Culture

					NCCU maintains extensive exchange and collaboration relationships with universities in Turkey, including Bilkent University, Kadir Has University, Koc University, Istanbul University, and Sabanci University. In addition to about 80 million Turkish speaking population in Turkey, there are a lot more Turkic ethnics spreading through Northwest provinces as well as regions in Central Asia, Western Asia and Eastern Europe. Because of frequent changes of Turkic ethnics and its expansive spread, their language and development of history caught the attention of Western scholars. Therefore, it brought about the rise of Turcology. Renowned colleges in Europe and America have graduate schools of Turcology and they hold academic seminars periodically. To Respond to the rise of Turcology, First established in 1990 to respond to the increasing strategic importance of Turkey, the Department cultivates Turkish linguistic and cultural competence through language training and courses on Turkish history, geography, politics, and social studies, preparing students for careers in commerce, diplomacy and academics.

The group met with local environmental advocacy organization Kumamoto Kankyō Shikōkai and assembly member Iwata Tomoko (third from the right), and toxicologist Mr. Fujiwara Toshikazu (sixth from the right), a long-standing voice on issues spanning Japan's atomic bombing legacy, nuclear disasters, industrial history, and environmental justice, had deep conversation and exchange the impact of the Semiconductor Industry in Taiwan and Japan. (Source: Michelle Then)

The team also visited the office of Anesis Group and conducted interviews with President Yabuuchi Mayumi (fifth from the left) and real estate division manager Murakami Takayori (sixth from the left), exchanging insights and observations on local real estate trends. (Source: Anesis Group)

(Source: Michelle Then)

The team visited a newly completed residential developments by local developer Anesis Group to discuss and exchange perspectives on housing and living cultures in Taiwan and Japan. (Source: Michelle Then)

The team also visited the office of Anesis Group and conducted interviews with President Yabuuchi Mayumi (fifth from the left) and real estate division manager Murakami Takayori (sixth from the left), exchanging insights and observations on local real estate trends. (Source: Anesis Group)

			Date :
			 2026-07-02 

			Department : 
			International College of Innovation

【Article by International College of Innovation】

Associate Professor Chen Hung-Ying of National Chengchi University's International College of Innovation (ICI) led an interdisciplinary student team on a six-day immersive field visit as an international academic exchange program in Kumamoto, Japan, from June 14 to 19, 2026. The visit was conducted in connection with the National Science and Technology Council (NSTC)-funded research project "Remaking the Technopolis" which examines housing supply and environmental transformation in communities surrounding science and technology parks. The program sought to deeply integrate research practice with pedagogical experience by bringing together students from multiple departments and universities for collaborative fieldwork.

The cross-university study group comprised students from ICI, the Department of Land Economics, and the College of Communication, working alongside faculty and students from Kyushu University's School of Interdisciplinary Studies. 

Prior to departure, the group completed two online workshops and two in-depth online interviews, drawing on the expertise of international urban and rural researchers as well as Kumamoto-based scholars to build a shared foundational framework for the field investigations.

The six-day program was structured around two main axes: field surveys and institutional visits. On the ground, students observed and documented a wide range of environments — from rural irrigation channels to semiconductor manufacturing facilities, from residential plots adjacent to burial grounds that reflect distinctive local land ethics, to peri-urban landscapes where diesel exhaust and construction dust defined the sensory experience. During the latter half of the program, the team shifted to institutional engagement. The group visited the Kumamoto Prefectural Assembly, met with local environmental advocacy organization Kumamoto Kankyō Shikōkai and assembly member Iwata Tomoko, and held in-depth conversations with toxicologist Mr. Fujiwara Toshikazu, a long-standing voice on issues spanning Japan's atomic bombing legacy, nuclear disasters, industrial history, and environmental justice.

In the area of housing market research, the team visited newly completed residential developments by local developer Anesis Group and conducted interviews with President Yabuuchi Mayumi and real estate division manager Murakami Takayori. These conversations enabled a close comparative analysis of the structural differences between Japanese and Taiwanese housing cultures since 1992 — including sharply divergent social understandings of housing as either ‘asset’ or ‘tool’, and broader questions of housing loan policy, market accessibility, and intergenerational housing justice.

The program demonstrated the productive synergies of NCCU's interdisciplinary pedagogy: students from the Department of Land Economics contributed grounded knowledge of Japan’s national spatial planning frameworks and environmental impact assessment regulations; Communication students took charge of visual documentation; and ICI students explored the role of cross-cultural mediation in international professional contexts. The participation of Professor Li Xiaoyan and her student from Kyushu University's Faculty of Arts and Science for Co-Creation brought real-time cross-cultural perspective into the field, forging research friendships and embodying the spirit of international co-learning. The team also paid a visit to ICI alumni working in Kumamoto's technology sector, bridging the pedagogical space of the classroom with the lived realities of alumni careers.

ICI has long been committed to grounding digital and technological development in humanistic and social literacy, and to extending the work of knowledge inquiry and production beyond the campus into live practice. This Kumamoto field program stands as a concrete expression of that commitment. Professor Chen reflected that the significance of immersive fieldwork lies not only in knowledge production, but in enabling students to measure the land with their own bodies — to sense environmental change and to encounter the distinct ethical frameworks through which different communities relate to their environments. From sensory experience to conceptual understanding, the study trip aimed to cultivate sensitivity and awareness to spatial injustice and environmental transformation. Findings from the research will be integrated into ongoing course design and future collaborative publication projects involving both faculty and students.

			Date :

			Department : 
			Master’s Program in Global Communication and Innovation Technology

【Article by GCIT 】 

Assistant Professor Tim Chun-Hao Chang of National Chengchi University’s Master’s Program in Global Communication and Innovation Technology (GCIT) represented the program at the 2026 Annual Conference of the International Association for Media and Communication Research (IAMCR), held at the University of Galway in Ireland from June 28 to July 2, 2026.

During the conference, Chang introduced GCIT’s educational vision, distinctive curriculum, and international development strategy to scholars from around the world, further enhancing the program’s international visibility.

Chang highlighted GCIT’s interdisciplinary approach, which integrates expertise and resources from communication, information technology, law, and the humanities and social sciences. He also presented the program’s educational model, which emphasizes English-medium instruction (EMI), the application of digital media and innovative technologies, industry–academia collaboration, and project-based learning.

During his visit, Chang met with Professor Paula Saukko of Loughborough University, Director of Research and Innovation for Criminology, Sociology and Social Policy in the School of Social Sciences and Humanities; Distinguished Professor Katie Ellis of Curtin University, Director of the Centre for Culture and Technology in the School of Media, Creative Arts and Social Inquiry; and Professor Panayiota Tsatsou of the Sir Lenny Henry Centre for Media Diversity at Birmingham City University.

Chang introduced GCIT’s curriculum and educational achievements and engaged in in-depth discussions with the scholars on digital inclusion, disability and media studies, artificial intelligence, and communication education. These meetings aimed to establish foundations for future collaboration, including inviting international scholars to teach courses or deliver guest lectures at NCCU, jointly developing short-term courses and workshops, and expanding opportunities for overseas internships, short-term study programs, and international research collaboration.

In addition to meeting with scholars and exploring potential partnerships, Chang presented his research on the audio-description needs and media accessibility experiences of people with visual impairments in Taiwan. His presentation showcased GCIT’s academic strengths in innovative technology, communication research, and social engagement to the international academic community.

The visit brought together program promotion, international exchange, and academic presentation. It marked an important milestone in GCIT’s ongoing efforts to strengthen overseas internship opportunities, develop international short-term courses, and advance cross-border teaching and research collaboration.

			Date :

			Department : 
			Master’s Program in Global Communication and Innovation Technology

【Article by GCIT】

Professor Edson C. Tandoc Jr. of Nanyang Technological University (NTU), Singapore, made a return visit to the Master’s program in Global Communication and Innovation Technology (GCIT) from July 8 to 25, 2026, to teach a three-week, English-taught summer intensive course titled “AI, Media, and Information Integrity.” The course examines the interplay between artificial intelligence and the contemporary media environment, guiding students to explore how AI is transforming the production, dissemination, and reception of information, as well as the challenges it poses to media trust, information integrity, and democratic societies.

Professor Tandoc is a faculty member at NTU’s Wee Kim Wee School of Communication and Information (WKWSCI). He also serves as the school’s Associate Chair for Research and Director of the Center for Information Integrity and the Internet (IN-Cube). His research focuses on journalism and communication, misinformation and disinformation, digital platforms, and the impact of artificial intelligence on the media industry and the public information environment. Following his visit to GCIT in 2025, during which he conducted a workshop and delivered a public lecture, Professor Tandoc returned this year to further strengthen academic exchange between the two institutions in the areas of AI, media, and information integrity.

The course covers a broad range of topics, including the history and theoretical foundations of AI, media ecology, applications of AI in journalism and advertising, the creative industries, deepfakes and misinformation, and AI and mental health. It attracted students from GCIT as well as the departments of psychology, radio and television, and Chinese literature, along with international students. Their diverse academic and cultural backgrounds enriched classroom discussions and fostered interdisciplinary and cross-cultural exchange.

In addition to Professor Tandoc, several scholars from NTU’s Wee Kim Wee School of Communication and Information contributed guest lectures to the course. Associate Professor Chen Lou and Assistant Professor Andrew Prahl discussed the applications of generative AI in public relations and advertising, as well as consumer perceptions of AI-generated content. Assistant Professor Pei-Sze Chow examined how generative AI is transforming practices in the creative industries. Associate Professor Saifuddin Ahmed focused on deepfakes, misinformation governance, and the current development of AI. Nanyang Assistant Professor Renwen Zhang explored human–AI interaction, algorithmic risks, and the potential effects of AI on mental health. Drawing on their respective areas of expertise, the guest speakers helped students develop a more comprehensive understanding of the opportunities and challenges AI presents for media and society.

Professor Tammy Lin, Director of GCIT, emphasized that as AI continues to reshape global communication and media, the program remains committed to cultivating students’ international perspectives, interdisciplinary capabilities, and critical thinking skills. Professor Tandoc’s visit and the NTU faculty team’s online lectures strengthened international academic collaboration while providing students with access to the latest research and industry insights.

(Photo by OIC)

Prof. Su poses for a photo with Prof. Géraldine Mühlmann, representative of Paris-Panthéon-Assas University. The two sides reached a positive consensus to formally launch discussions on a student exchange agreement this autumn. (Photo OIC)

The dialogue focused on future blueprints for co-teaching and English-taught program promotions. (Photo by OIC)

Prof. Su visits Université Sorbonne Nouvelle, posing for a photo with Vice President for International Relations Françoise Lavocat (second from right) and international affairs staff to highlight the friendly higher education ties between the two universities. (Photo OIC)

			Date :
			 2026-07-20 

			Department : 
			Office of International Cooperation (OIC)

【Article by OIC】

To deepen academic cooperation with its partner institution, Sciences Po Paris, National Chengchi University (NCCU) has selected 10 talented students to participate in the Sciences Po Summer School. Supported by the Ministry of Education's bilingual initiative, the student delegation was accompanied by Professor Cho-Hsin Su, Vice President for International Cooperation. Following the summer school's commencement, Professor Su embarked on a week-long visit to the Taipei Representative Office and several top-tier French universities to expand NCCU’s collaborative blueprint in European higher education.

During the intensive visit from June 29 to July 3, Professor Su met with representatives from Sciences Po Paris, Paris 1 Panthéon-Sorbonne University, Paris-Panthéon-Assas University (Paris II), the National Institute for Oriental Languages and Civilizations (Inalco), and Université Sorbonne Nouvelle (Paris 3). The discussions led to substantial progress on various areas, including student exchange agreements, English-taught course alignments, dual degree programs, short-term summer programs, and international student support systems.

The tour began at Sciences Po Paris. Founded in 1872, the institution consistently ranks among the top three globally in politics and international studies. The international affairs representative for the Asia-Pacific region warmly welcomed the delegation and commended the outstanding quality of NCCU students. The representative noted that in recent years, Taiwan and NCCU have become highly popular exchange destinations for their students, leading to vibrant two-way mobility. The representative also expressed gratitude to NCCU for sending 10 talented students to their summer program this year, looking forward to advancing future academic collaborations.

At Paris 1 Panthéon-Sorbonne University, a prominent institution established in 1971 with roots tracking back to the 13th-century University of Paris, Professor Su met with the international relations team. The university highlighted its expanding catalog of English-taught courses, stretching from economics and politics into modern art history, alongside its "Bienvenue en France" initiative, which assists international students with local integration. Both sides discussed administrative internationalization exchanges and evaluated the potential for future dual degree programs.

Positive developments were achieved at Paris-Panthéon-Assas University (Paris II), renowned throughout Europe for its elite law school. The representative from Paris II stated that the university is actively preparing a cooperation agreement with NCCU. Discussions on a formal student exchange contract are scheduled to begin this autumn, aiming to launch the exchange program next year.

At Inalco, a world-class institution for languages and civilizations dating back to 1669, the dialogue focused on innovative educational synergy. As a pillar of the French elite education system that trains a significant portion of the country's diplomats, Inalco leads the nation in Chinese language research while providing French programs for international students. Showing strong interest in NCCU's diverse English-taught programs, the representative expressed a commitment to promoting exchange opportunities at NCCU to their students.

The final visit took place at Université Sorbonne Nouvelle (Paris 3), a major center for contemporary culture, literature, and communication studies. The university's Vice President and the international affairs team hosted the meeting, outlining their multilingual advisory services and supportive environment for international students. During the visit, Professor Su also met with a Sorbonne Nouvelle student who is scheduled to depart for an exchange semester at NCCU, demonstrating the warm welcome awaiting French students in Taipei.

This successful delegation not only solidifies NCCU’s relationships with its existing European partners but also opens doors for new collaborations in dual degrees and short-term study initiatives. Moving forward, NCCU remains committed to fostering a diverse, global campus environment and advancing higher education ties between Taiwan and France.

			Date :

			Department : 
			Office of International Cooperation (OIC)

【Article by OIC】

Funded by Ministry of Education, Prof. Chien-Wu Hsueh, Section Chief of the Mainland Affairs Section, along with Senior Regional Manager Ms. Kelly Wang, at the Office of International Cooperation (OIC), National Chengchi University (NCCU) recently led a group of 14 well-selected NCCU students to attend 2026 International Summer Semester at Sungkyunkwan University (SKKU) in Seoul, South Korea, as part of its ongoing internationalization and bilingual education initiatives. During this month-long summer program, NCCU students can freely select three courses based on their academic interests from fields like Business & Economy, Social Sciences & Humanities, Computer & Data Science, Engineering, to Korean Language Studies. The courses were taught not only by faculty from SKKU but also by guest professors from renowned international institutions such as the University of South Carolina and Michigan State University, etc.

The initiative highlights the long-standing relationship between NCCU and SKKU, which dates back to 1964 when the two institutions signed their first academic cooperation agreement, making each other mutually their very first partnership in the world. Today, SKKU is ranked 126th globally in the 2026 QS World University Rankings, receives substantial investment from the Samsung Group, and remains one of the top five universities for corporate recruitment in South Korea. 

During this trip, Prof. Hsueh and the student group also visited the Taipei Mission in Korea and met with the Director of the Education Division Cheng-Kie Cheng, Secretary Jing-Yi Wong, and Ms. Cheng Han-Fei. The discussion focused on the current status of educational exchange activities between Taiwan and South Korea, as well as English-Medium Instruction (EMI) policies. Director Cheng noted that while the South Korean government actively promotes English education through initiatives like "English Villages," its universities face challenges similar to Taiwan regarding a shortage of qualified EMI faculty. He also shared observations on the competitive nature of early-childhood English education in South Korea, where children as young as 4 years old sometimes need to take competitive entrance examinations to enter private English immersion kindergartens.

In addition to the summer program activities at SKKU, the OIC representatives also visited several other partners in Seoul, including Hanyang University, Seoul National University, and Korea University to discuss ways to strengthen collaborations. At SKKU, discussions focused on faculty exchange mechanism and expanding future cooperation in summer programs. At Hanyang University, the two sides discussed the possibility of co-hosting future summer modules in Taiwan, drawing on Hanyang's previous experience with Japanese and domestic universities. At Seoul National University, both parties expressed a mutual desire to actively encourage joint research projects while at Korea University, the discussion circulate around reviewing incentives to encourage more Korea University students to study in Taiwan, and exploring opportunities for faculty exchange.

Before concluding the trip, the OIC representatives met with NCCU exchange and degree-seeking students currently studying at Yonsei University, Dongguk University, and the University of Seoul to learn about their academic progress and future career plans. The OIC stated that the university will continue to coordinate international resources to provide further learning and research opportunities for NCCU faculty and students.

			Date :

【 Article by the College of Communication】

The College of Communication at National Chengchi University (NCCU) and the Korean Advertising Society (KAS) jointly hosted the 2026 KAS–NCCU Global Advertising Conference on July 7–8 at NCCU's Center for Public and Business Administration Education. Held under the theme "Advertising in the Age of AI and Platforms: Transparency, Creativity, and Consumer Experience," the conference brought together advertising and communication scholars, graduate students, and industry professionals from Taiwan, Korea, the United States, the Netherlands, the United Kingdom, and Hong Kong to examine how artificial intelligence is reshaping advertising research, brand communication, and consumer experience. The event marked not only the first global advertising conference jointly organized by NCCU's College of Communication and KAS, but also the first time KAS had held its Global Colloquium outside Korea, underscoring NCCU's growing role as a platform for international collaboration in advertising research.

Reflecting the conference's commitment to connecting research with industry practice, the keynote address was delivered by Sega Cheng, Co-Founder and Chairman of iKala. In his talk, "Agentic AI and the Transformation of Marketing Communication," Cheng drew on his experience at the forefront of the technology sector to offer a firsthand perspective on the rapidly evolving AI landscape, how it is transforming business and marketing, and the opportunities it presents for organizations. His keynote provided participants with valuable industry insights while encouraging broader reflection on the future of advertising and marketing communication in the age of AI.

The conference also featured a Global Leaders Panel, moderated by Dr. Jhih-Syuan (Elaine) Lin, Associate Dean for Graduate Studies and Chair of the Department of Advertising at NCCU. The panel brought together Dr. Yongjun Sung, President of the Korean Advertising Society and Professor of Psychology at Korea University; Dr. Jameson Hayes, Past President of the American Academy of Advertising and Professor of Advertising at the University of South Carolina; Dr. Sophie Boerman, Board Member of the European Advertising Academy and Associate Professor of Persuasive Communication at Wageningen University & Research; Dr. Fuyuan Shen, Founding Member of the Asia Pacific Advertising Academy and Chair and Donald P. Bellisario Professor of Advertising at Penn State University; and Mr. Ling-Te Lee, Associate Director of AI Product Development at Dentsu. Drawing on perspectives from academia and industry across Asia, North America, and Europe, the panel examined the implications of AI for consumers, brands, advertising research, and education, while considering how the field can adapt its research, professional practice, and talent development to the changes ahead.

In addition to the keynote address and panel discussion, the conference featured 16 research presentations by scholars and graduate students from institutions including Korea University, Yonsei University, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, and Queen Mary University of London, among others. The papers explored transparency and authenticity in AI advertising, generative AI and creativity, personalization and consumer experience, and the growing role of platforms, algorithms, and agentic AI. The paper sessions highlighted the breadth of emerging research on advertising in the age of AI and provided an international forum for scholarly exchange.

Dr. Lin noted, "NCCU's College of Communication has long been committed to connecting Taiwan with the international communication research community. Co-hosting this conference with the Korean Advertising Society marks another important step in that effort, strengthening collaboration with international advertising organizations, universities, and research communities around the world." Looking ahead, the College will continue to advance international research collaboration, teaching partnerships, and graduate education. It will also expand opportunities for early-career scholars and graduate students to participate in international conferences, collaborative research, and academic exchange, further strengthening the College's role within the international communication research community.

			Date :

			Department : 
			Office of International Cooperation (OIC)

【Article by OIC】

To deepen academic cooperation with Sciences Po Paris, one of its key partner institutions, National Chengchi University (NCCU) has selected 10 outstanding students from a competitive pool of applicants across the university. Financed by a Ministry of Education subsidy, the selected students will participate in the Sciences Po Summer School. The delegation comprises both undergraduate and postgraduate students from a diverse range of academic disciplines including Diplomacy, Law, Communication, Ethnology, English, and Japanese, showcasing the depth of NCCU's cross-disciplinary talent. Led by Associate Vice President of the Office of International Cooperation Professor Cho-Hsin Su, the delegation visited the Taipei Representative Office in France on June 29. They were received by Lu Mei-Chen, Director of the Education Division, for an in-depth discussion on the current state and future prospects of academic diplomacy and Taiwan France higher education cooperation, kicking off the study tour.

During the meeting, Director Lu pointed out that as interactions between Taiwan and France grow increasingly close, the two sides have gradually initiated substantive cooperation across multiple fields, including technology, education, and culture. In recent years, a growing number of Taiwanese enterprises have invested and established factories in France. Coupled with Taiwan's world-leading semiconductor technology, many French universities have proactively expressed keen interest in establishing deeper partnerships with Taiwanese higher education institutions to co-cultivate a new generation of professional talent. She noted that educational links between Taiwan and France are transitioning from individual inter-collegiate exchanges toward systemic, long-term strategic cooperation.

During the exchange, the NCCU student delegates enthusiastically asked questions and engaged in lively discussions regarding France's political landscape, the current state of higher education, and the career paths and personal experiences of overseas diplomats. Among the team members, many aspire to join the civil service and hope to be stationed abroad in the future, sharing a deep curiosity and passion for the realities of  diplomatic work. Director Lu responded insightfully to each query, encouraging the students to make the most of their journey. She inspired them to immerse themselves in France’s critical-thinking culture, foster their own unique insights through academic exchange, and leverage this one-month study tour to enrich their long-term career paths and global horizons.

Director Lu also praised NCCU for its sustained dedication to international exchange, particularly with French institutions. Noting that NCCU President Li Tsai-yen headed a delegation to France last year, she recognized NCCU as a key driver in strengthening Taiwan-France higher education cooperation. Prof. Su added that as a key think tank for European Union studies in Taiwan, NCCU has continuously deepened cooperation with its French partner institutions in recent years. This has resulted not only in steady growth in the volume of exchanges but also a comprehensive upgrade in the quality of cooperation. The selection of these talented students for the Sciences Po Summer School is a clear demonstration of NCCU’s long-term commitment to international collaboration.

Looking ahead to the coming month, the ten students will join over 200 participants from more than 60 countries at Sciences Po. Under the guidance of distinguished international faculty, they will engage in academic exchange, expand their international horizons, and build global networks within a multicultural environment. Prof. Su expressed her hope that this journey will not only enhance the students' professional capabilities but also further advance Taiwan-France educational exchange, strengthening NCCU’s long-term presence and engagement in Europe.

            證件（正本及1份影本），至政治大學辦理（文山區校本部，因校區地坪將施工，驗證地點確認後另行公告並通知）；若委託他人代辦，請附委託書

            及被委託人之身分證明文件正本。

       2. 應屆畢業生如因個別因素（如暑修、境外學歷尚在駐外單位驗證等）尚未能取得符合報考資格之學歷證件，應先繳交已蓋註冊章戳之學生證

           （或在學證明）及填具切結書，並提供延長切結證明文件，經本校同意得延長切結時間（至多延長至115學年度本校開學日） 。逾期未驗證

          者，即以自願放棄入學資格論。

一、本項考試錄取生「報到分發結果名單」請點選附件查詢。

二、注意事項：

（一）錄取生經報到分發即取得本校入學資格，不得以任何理由要求更改分發學系。

（二）獲分發之錄取生如欲放棄入學資格者，應填妥附檔「放棄入學資格聲明書」(點選下方連結)，經父母（或監護人）簽名或蓋章後，於115年5月18日前（郵戳為憑）以掛號郵寄至「116971臺北市文山指南郵局第365號信箱 國立政治大學教務處綜合業務組」；如未於上述期限內向本校聲明放棄者，當學年度不得報考大學考試入學分發招生；如已獲大學或技專校院各入學管道錄取者，應繳交原錄取學校之放棄聲明書，否則一經查明，即取消本項考試錄取資格。

（三）逾放棄截止日(即115年5月18日)，因特殊事由欲放棄入學資格者，仍應向本校聲明放棄。放棄後是否得報名參加其他入學管道招生，悉依該入學管道之招生簡章規定辦理。

（四）經「公告分發之錄取生」及「已遞補之備取生」，應於規定時間至本校辦理現場驗證。未辦理驗證者，視同放棄入學資格，不得以任何理由要求補救措施；驗證時間、地點另行通知。

（五）錄取生經繳費註冊入學後，其應修學分、科目(含補修)及畢業資格取得等事項，悉依本校學則及各該學系之規定辦理。

（六）經報到分發之錄取生，於本校修業期間，須配合參加該運動代表隊訓練。

（七）有關新生入學注意事項，請於6月底至本校教務處網頁（網址: [https://aca.nccu.edu.tw/zh/](https://aca.nccu.edu.tw/zh/)）點選「新生服務網」參閱。

一、本招生不販售紙本簡章，請自行網頁瀏覽或列印，報名前請務必詳閱簡章。

二、報名方式、日期及報名流程(以下各項逾時不受理)：

（一）國防專班：採網路報名、通訊寄件，報名請至本校「招生專區」/點選「招生網路報名系統」（網址：https://enroll.nccu.edu.tw/EXAM/）。

1.網路報名取得繳費帳號：自115年7月21日上午9時起至8月6日中午12時止。 

2.網路報名登錄資料：自115年7月21日上午9時起至8月6日下午3時止。

3.審查資料繳交截止日：115年8月6日下午7時止，依專班學程分則之「資料繳交方式」規定辦理。

4.報名流程：

(1)於報名系統取得繳費帳號。

(2)於報名系統線上以信用卡、金融卡繳款、或至全國金融機構自動櫃員機(ATM)繳費、第一銀行臨櫃繳款（擇一方式繳費）。

(3)於報名系統填寫個人基本資料，完成報名後下載PDF報名表自行存檔。

(4)依專班規定繳交報名所需相關表件。

(5)有關網路報名系統操作介面請詳下方連結參閱。

（二）領導決策專班指參教育組：採通訊方式報名

1.報名期間：自115年7月21日起至8月6日下午7時止。

2.繳件方式：請將報名表及專班規定所需繳交資料，依下列方式擇一辦理。

(1)掛號郵寄：於115年7月21日至8月2日下午7時前，將報名資料以掛號寄達本校行政管理碩士學程辦公室。

(2)現場收件：於115年8月1日上午9時至下午5時、8月3日至8月6日每日上午9時至下午7時，將報名資料送達本校行政管理碩士學程辦公室。

三、若有疑問，請於上班時間（08:30~12:00；13:30~17:00）洽詢本校教務處綜合業務組(02)2938-7892、2938-7893。

一、本項考試成績單於115年5月7日（星期四）以平信寄出。

二、本校另提供網路成績查詢系統，網址：[https://examscore.nccu.edu.tw/Login](https://examscore.nccu.edu.tw/Login)，相關流程請詳下方連結說明。

三、考生對本項考試成績有疑義，得申請成績複查，請於115年5月19日(星期二)前向本校提出申請。

1、申請方式：一律以網路方式申請。欲申請成績複查之考生請至成績複查系統（網址：[https://examscore.nccu.edu.tw/Login](https://examscore.nccu.edu.tw/Login)）

   點選欲複查之科目，並依系統所產生之繳費帳號完成繳費（每科目複查費新臺幣50元），口頭查詢概不受理。

2、複查結果請自行至成績複查系統查詢，不寄發書面通知。

3、申請複查僅限試卷內有無漏閱、未評閱及卷面分數成績加總有誤及登錄錯誤為範圍，不得要求試卷重閱。各系所學程之「資料審查」

   或「面試」不得要求重審或提供評分等有關資料。

四、若有疑義，請於上班時間洽本校教務處綜合業務組（02）2938-7892、2938-7893。

[成績查詢操作說明.pdf](https://www.nccu.edu.tw/app/index.php?Action=downloadfile&file=WVhSMFlXTm9MelkxTDNCMFlWODFOVE13WHpFM016VXpNVEJmTnpNek9UWXVjR1Jt&fname=WSGG50FGYWDC41HHEDLKKPLOWWJGWT2434UWMPNPTXID0040QKA4LOB4WW54NKOKROPOGGOOA404PO14MKSWTSXWB0MOICHC41YTXWTSPOA4CDUWIGGC24DCGCLK0115JCLKSXHGTWFGSWHCUS30A110&cg=88)

一、本校「116學年度僑生及港澳生學士班【個人自薦】單獨招生」不販售紙本簡章，請自行網頁瀏覽或列印，報名前請務必詳閱簡章。（請點選下方連結參閱）

二、推薦資格及重要時程如下：（臺灣時間，逾時不受理）

報名時間：2026年10月8日至11月16日（2026年11月16日下午3時前完成上網報名，同日下午5時前完成網路上傳審查資料）。

審查結果通知：2027年1月21日

公告錄取名單：2027年1月28日下午2時

報到時間：2027年1月28日下午2時至2月15日下午5時止

公告入學分發結果名單：2027年2月18日

三、本校「116學年度僑生及港澳生學士班單獨招生」報名方式一律採網路報名及網路上傳審查資料電子檔案。（詳請參閱簡章第7~8頁）

       審查資料：個人基本資料、學歷證明資料、個人學經歷及生涯規劃表、其他有利審查資料。

 1.  僑生於個人基本資料中需包含「華裔身分認定文件」，如無法提供可改由繳交「國內單招學校辦理華裔身分認定初審檢核表」，請點選下方檔案使用。

 2.  僑生繳交學歷證明資料需經[駐外機構](https://www.mofa.gov.tw/OverseasOffice.aspx?n=168&sms=87)或[僑務委員會指定之保薦單位](https://www.ocac.gov.tw/OCAC/Pages/List.aspx?nodeid=1873)驗證。

 3. 「個人學經歷及生涯規劃表」、「其他有利審查資料」請點選下方檔案填寫。

四、本項招生設有僑生及港澳生新生入學獎學金，鼓勵學生就讀本校：

 1.  全額獎學金：學雜費全免及每學年核發生活津貼新台幣十五萬元。

 2.  半額獎學金：學雜費全免。

獎學金由本校審查委員就報名招生考生中擇優選取，如有獲獎將於公告錄取名單時主動通知。

五、為獎勵優秀僑生來讀本校，政大與僑務委員會聯名推出「頂尖及傑出僑生入學獎學金」，相關訊息請參閱[僑務委員會網站](https://www.ocac.gov.tw/OCAC/Pages/VDetail.aspx?nodeid=4496&pid=13194588)：

 1.  頂尖僑生入學獎學金：每學年新臺幣26萬元，採續領審核機制。

 2.  傑出僑生入學獎學金：每學年新臺幣10萬元，採續領審核機制。

 符合申請資格之僑生請自行向各駐外館處提出申請。

(四) 驗證資料：

1. 身分證件：「僑生」繳驗僑居地居留證件（身分證、護照）或中華民國護照暨僑居身分加簽、「港澳生」繳驗港澳地區永久居留證件（身分證、護照）之正、影本。

2. 高中畢業證書：經我政府駐外機構驗證或由僑務主管機關指定單位（含僑務委員會指定之保薦單位及海外華僑文教服務中心）核驗之高中畢業證書（或同等學力證明文件）正本。【各地臺校畢業生免繳駐外單位驗證文件】

3. 高中歷年成績單：經我政府駐外機構驗證或由僑務主管機關指定之單位（含僑務委員會指定之保薦單位及海外華僑文教服務中心）核驗之高中歷年成績單之正本。【各地臺校畢業生免繳駐外單位驗證文件】

◎ 上述畢業證書及成績單如為中、英文以外之語文，應加附中文或英文譯本。

◎ 無法於上述時間辦理者，請於9月10日(四)前，於上班時間（08:30~12:00；13:30~17:00）至行政大樓四樓教務處綜合業務組補行查驗。

(五) 駐外館處及僑務主管機關指定單位資訊： 

1. 各國駐外館處資訊可至外交部網頁http://www.mofa.gov.tw/ 點選「[國家與地區](https://www.mofa.gov.tw/CountryAreaInfo.aspx?casn=5&n=5&sms=33)」項下查詢。

2. 僑務主管機關指定單位為僑務委員會提供的保薦單位，請至僑委會網站http://www.ocac.gov.tw/點選「僑生服務」/「[保薦單位名單](https://www.ocac.gov.tw/OCAC/Pages/VDetail.aspx?nodeid=1873&pid=79423246)」查詢。

◎ 如畢業中學為保薦單位(如寬柔中學)，仍需完成保薦單位核驗畢業證書與歷年成績單之程序。

二、正取生：如有調移志願需求，請於6月1日中午前填寫「正取調移學系申請表」（請點選下方連結），逾期不予受理。調移學系分發說明請詳「正取調移及備取遞補學系分發說明」（請點選下方連結）。[申請表請於6月1日中午前拍照存成JPG(或PDF)檔email至oaa@nccu.edu.tw](mailto:oaa@nccu.edu.tw)信箱，繳交後來電確認（教務處綜合業務組 02-29387892、29387893）。調移結果於6月13日上午10時公告於本校「[招生專區](http://www.nccu.edu.tw/zh_tw/admissions/undergraduate)」。

三、獲分發錄取生如參加其他入學管道而獲錄取者，應至其他入學管道之錄取大學報到前，完成聲明放棄入學資格，否則一經發現，即取消本招生分發校系之錄取資格。惟115年6月11日統一分發結果公告前，已於其他入學管道錄取且完成報到者，不影響本招生之獲分發錄取資格。

六、獲分發之錄取生應於註冊時繳交學校畢業證書，或依教育部發布之「大學入學同等學力認定標準」規定繳交相關同等學力證明，否則取消入學資格，不准註冊入學。

一、本項考試採「網路報名」，報名網址：[https://enroll.nccu.edu.tw/EXAM/](https://enroll.nccu.edu.tw/EXAM/)。

二、報名方式、日期：(以下各項皆逾時不受理)

(一)網路取得報名繳費帳號期間：

自115年5月7日(四)上午9時起至5月13日(三)中午12時止。

(二)網路登錄報名資料期間：

自115年5月7日(四)上午9時起至5月13日(三)下午3時止。

(三)依報考學系規定上傳審查資料期間：

自115年5月7日(四)上午9時起至5月13日(三)下午5時止。

(四)特種生(退伍軍人及運動成績優良學生)掛號郵寄審查資料：

自115年5月7日(四)至5月13日(三)止(以郵戳為憑，逾期不受理)。

三、報名流程：

（一）於報名系統取得繳費帳號。

（二）於報名系統線上以信用卡、金融卡繳款、或至全國金融機構自動提款機（ATM）繳費、第一銀行臨櫃繳款（擇一方式繳費）。

（三）於報名系統填寫個人基本資料，完成報名後下載PDF報名表自行存檔。

（四）依學系規定網路上傳審查資料，內容請參閱招生簡章學系分則。

（五）特種身分考生(退伍軍人、運動成績優良學生)及持境外學歷考生應掛號寄繳相關證明文件。

四、若有疑問，請於上班時間（08:30~12:00；13:30~17:00）洽本校教務處綜合業務組(02)2938-7892、2938-7893。

二、報名方式、日期(以下各項皆逾時不受理)：

（一）網路取得報名繳費帳號期間：自114年9月30日上午9時起至10月14日中午12時止。

二、獲分發錄取生請於115年3月3日（星期二）中午12:00前以傳真方式辦理報到。

（一）傳真報到繳驗證件：

（1）最高學歷（力）證件。

（2）國民身分證或其他相當之身分證件。

（3）填妥之「報到意願同意書」（請點選下方連結）。

（二）傳真號碼：（02）2938-7495。傳真後請於上班時間來電確認，聯絡電話：（02）2938-7892或（02）2938-7893。

（三）逾期未完成報到手續之分發錄取生，本校得取消分發錄取資格，分發錄取生不得異議。

三、分發錄取生如同時獲得115學年度四技二專技優保送入學招生分發錄取資格，須擇一辦理報到，違者取消特殊選才入學聯合招生之分發錄取資格。

五、獲分發之錄取生且已完成辦理報到者，如欲參加本學年度四技二專技優保送入學、科技校院繁星計畫聯合推薦甄選入學、科技校院日間部四年制申請入學聯合招生、四技二專之技優甄審入學、甄選入學、日間部聯合登記分發或其他各四技二專學校及所有大學校院之入學招生者，應於「115學年度科技校院四年制及專科學校二年制特殊選才入學聯合招生簡章」規定時間填妥簡章附錄十一「[已報到錄取生放棄錄取聲明書](https://www.jctv.ntut.edu.tw/downloads/115/s42/A11.pdf)」（請點連結），向本校聲明放棄錄取及入學資格，否則一律不得報名其他各四技二專學校及所有大學校院之入學招生，違者取消其本招生錄取及入學資格【報到錄取生聲明放棄錄取入學資格截止時間為115年3月3日（星期二）12：00前】。

			日期 :
			 2025-11-01 

			單位 : 
			秘書處

【校訊記者吳妤潔報導】

國立政治大學一年一度的盛事「包種茶節」系所博覽會今（1）日在政大校區盛大登場，吸引全台約1,800名高中生熱情參與。各院系精心佈置攤位、熱心解說，並在舞臺區帶來充滿活力的表演，展現政大學子的創意與熱情。活動當天亦舉辦多場深度座談會，透過系所簡介與學長姐的經驗分享，協助高中生與家長深入了解各學系特色及未來就業前景。

今年包種茶節的主視覺以代表「數位與人文加乘」、「創造無限想像」的「X」字樣呈現，展現政大學生得以自身為軸心，透過豐富的跨領域資源，自由探索、激發無限可能。在這裡，「X」不只是數學符號，更是學生實現自我、展現潛能以及突破框架的象徵。

校長李蔡彥表示，政大校風自由開放，學習制度富有彈性。學生不只能夠前往有興趣學習的系所就讀，更能夠透過「校學士」制度，創造屬於自己的學位。政大不論是在人文、科技、運動抑或國際上的豐沛資源，都會是第一志願的好選擇。李蔡彥也勉勵高中學子「設定目標之後就要勇往直前」，期待未來再次於校園相見。

本次活動除了號召校內37個系所參與外，串聯校際圖書、修課及國內外實習資源的台灣聯合大學系統，則由四校中的國立陽明交通大學、國立中央大學以及友校國立臺北藝術大學再度共襄盛舉。而政大運動產業文化學士學位學程（以下簡稱運動學程）更首度加入，攤位上掛著清晰可見的深藍色「Sport X」旗幟，不僅代表運動學程跨域連結的精神，更完美契合政大多元實踐的核心理念。

由於運動學程採對內招生形式，學程助教林怡璇說明，希望透過攤位介紹，增加高中生就讀政大的誘因；另一方面，也期待更多校內學生認識學程並參與其中。來自教育系的總召張張瑋倢分享，在課程之餘，學程也會辦理模擬記者會、台政運動學程交流會和國際交流等，希望招攬對運動領域有興趣的學生，未來能夠成為運動產業人才。目前，運動學程也正在籌辦運動文學獎，期待「用文字運動」，藉此推廣運動文化。文學獎設有高中組、大專組與政大人組，並預計於明年舉辦。

根據統計，中、南、東部名校包括新竹高中、蘭陽高中、彰化女中、文華高中等全臺上千名高中生參與。這次政大亦特別贈予前十所團體報名的學校，特製的壓克力「包中」御守。在開幕典禮中，校長李蔡彥及教務長林啓屏也加碼贈送御守給其他在場學子，祝福升學之路順遂、如願。

來自彰化女中的高三學生鄭心語、許庭榕分別想了解中文學系和法政學群，認為興趣和分數會是選擇大學的主要考量。聊到對政大的第一印象，鄭心語和許庭榕除了感受到本校學生的熱情，更不約而同笑說政大充滿了森林的氣息，很喜歡這樣的氛圍。

政大之聲實習廣播電邀請校長李蔡彥與教務長林啓屏對談。校長李蔡彥提到政大以自由開放的校風培育創意，他強調：「只有在自由的靈魂之下，才有好的創意與設計」。（攝影：秘書處）

午後細雨綿綿，人潮仍在攤位間穿。（攝影：秘書處）

			日期 :
			 2025-11-03 

			單位 : 
			秘書處

【校訊記者黃伊晨報導】

微涼的秋風拂過政大校門口，人潮沿著展攤徐徐湧動，笑語與廣播聲交織校園熱鬧景色。2025 年國立政治大學「包種茶節」於 11 月 1 日登場，山下各學院攤位串連師長與學生策劃的深度座談，吸引高中師生與民眾走進校園，近距離認識政大各院系的學習樣貌。

各系攤位設計巧思滿滿，透過互動遊戲與主題展示，呈現系所的多元特色與創意。教育系以「育見未來的你」為題，立起象徵引路之光的「燈塔」，並以航向藍白大海的船作為主視覺，象徵教育如同引路之光。總召王同學表示，高中生對「教育八大必修」與未來方向特別關心，「不少人直接問到中等教育與科目專長的規劃，能感覺他們想更深入了解教育系的養成。」

創新國際學院則由臺籍生與外籍生共同介紹「城市設計」、「永續與社會」、「全球治理」三大軌道，現場安排外籍學生與參觀者直接互動，讓大家第一眼就能感受到學院的國際組成與跨域氛圍。攤位以卡通動畫〈探險活寶〉為主題，總召陳同學表示，這個意象象徵探索與冒險的精神，「創國是一個新學院，學生需要不斷嘗試與發現，像探險一樣去認識自己在做什麼。這部卡通代表包容與勇氣，也很符合學院的特色。」希望參觀者能從中感受到學院開放而多元的氛圍。

CCA 商院生涯大使攤位結合商學院八個系所，打造「美式復古遊樂園」主題，以集點闖關串連八大系所，帶領高中生參與。資管系柳同學提及，諮詢桌與深度座談同步進行，「從科系介紹、學習歷程到出路，一次把高中生最常問的都講清楚。」

廣場一隅的 Open Studio 傳出音樂與訪談聲，政大之聲實習廣播電台依照慣例在校內架設開放式錄音棚。今年節目邀請校長李蔡彥與教務長林啓屏對談。李蔡彥提到，政大以自由開放的校風培育創意，他強調：「只有在自由的靈魂之下，才有好的創意與設計。」並以今年啟動的「校學士學程」回應時代變遷，鼓勵學生以「積木式修課」打造跨域能力。

林啟屏則表示，每年教務處規劃包種茶節，就是希望能讓高中生與家長親身感受政大的人文底蘊與學習環境。「每個攤位都逛過、收穫滿滿離開，才是最值得。」他也提醒，現場並設有台灣聯合大學系統與合作院校攤位，鼓勵同學把握跨校資源，並期盼來訪的高中生將來能把政大放在第一志願。

活動獲得高中生熱烈迴響。彰化女中黃同學說，法學院的大富翁遊戲讓她更熟悉法律名詞；台中二中陳同學分享，參加商學院說明會後，更清楚了解各系課程與出路。蘭陽女中的同學在創國學院試著與外籍生用英文對談，也留下深刻的印象。

午後細雨綿綿，人潮仍在攤位間穿梭，廣播聲與笑聲交織不斷——政大以開放與跨域，持續將大學的學習風景延伸至更廣的社群。

中大同學熱情介紹。（照片來源：台聯大辦公室）

陽明交大同學整齊劃一。（照片來源：台聯大辦公室）

中大同學熱情介紹。（照片來源：台聯大辦公室）

陽明交大同學整齊劃一。（照片來源：台聯大辦公室）

			日期 :
			 2025-11-03 

			單位 : 
			台聯大-政大辦公室

【台聯大校訊記者何則文報導】

國立政治大學一年一度的「包種茶節」日前盛大舉行，儘管天公不作美、陰雨綿綿，依舊澆不熄高中生的熱情。除了校內各系所總動員，作為「台灣聯合大學系統」（台聯大）夥伴的國立中央大學、國立陽明交通大學，也齊聚政大，向來訪高中生展現各自的學術特色與校園文化。

台聯大夥伴：中央、陽明交大 展現理工與人文特色

已連續三年受邀參與的中央大學，今年由教務處招生組的吳淑婷專員領軍。她表示，自政大三年前開始邀請台聯大夥伴學校以來，中央大學便年年參與。為呼應政大在社會科學領域的優勢，今年特別安排了中文系、英文系、資管系與數學系的學生隨行，希望能提供跨文、理、管學院的多元諮詢，讓社會組的學生也能看見中央大學在理工之外的豐富面貌。

中央大學提供了L夾、尺以及折疊扇作為贈品，並以詳盡的「學系介紹手冊」為主要文宣。吳淑婷專員特別提到，今年攤位也為新成立的「法律與政府學系」準備了簡介。她觀察到，高中生最常問的問題是「學校在哪裡」，顯見「中字輩」大學的地理位置常讓學生混淆；但也有許多學生問得非常深入，例如自然組學生詢問化材系的具體所學，或對中文系的課程內容感到好奇。

陽明交大攤位則由三位熱心的在校生負責，分別是電機系的張同學、生物科技系的吳同學，以及人社系的謝同學。已是第三年參加的吳同學笑稱自己經驗豐富，而張同學則是第一次參與。他們提到，今年的攤位準備學校的「總介紹」，給學生更全面的瞭解；贈品則包含鏡子、鑰匙圈、簡章和貼紙。不過，三名學生都感覺今年的雨勢較大，人流明顯不如往年，期待明年天公作美。

跨校印象：政大「活力十足」但也「總在下雨、一直爬山」

當被問及對政大的印象時，兩所學校的師生竟給出了驚人一致的答案：「每年來都在下雨」。陽明交大的吳同學表示，她連來三年都遇到下雨，且感覺「今年的雨特別大」；中央大學的吳淑婷專員也笑著證實，去年包種茶節是「風大」，今年則是「雨大」。

儘管天候陰晴不定，政大校園展現的充沛活力仍讓夥伴學校印象深刻。夥伴學校學生便驚嘆政大「超級有活力」，一早就有熱鬧的社團表演，這在自己學校是難以想像的景象，「我們學生比較靜，早上的校園都很安靜」。陽明交大的同學也認為，政大學生「感覺比較活潑」，校園氛圍與理工為主的交大校區截然不同。

而在校園地景上，各校感受也大相逕庭。陽明交大的學生覺得政大校區「很大、很空曠」，對比之下，他們形容交大校區「很小、很擠、建築物很多」。而常來政大找朋友的中央大學數學系同學則對政大的地形很有感，他苦笑著說：「為什麼要到朋友的教室或宿舍，要一直爬山？」不過他也稱讚台聯大系統的校際專車非常方便。中央大學的師長則對活動如此盛大感到佩服，認為這需要豐沛的資源與經費支持。期待明年能繼續交流。

一站式博覽會 盡覽各校多元風貌

「包種茶節」不僅是政大的年度盛事，更因「台聯大」夥伴中央大學、陽明交大的加入力挺，使其昇華為全臺灣最與眾不同的大學科系博覽會之一。來訪的高中生與家長均表示，僅需走一趟政大校園，便能一次飽覽各所頂尖大學的多元風貌，從社會科學、理工科技到設計，大幅拓展升學的視野與想像，成為包種茶節無可取代的獨特價值。

教務處同仁也認為，這種「強強聯手」的模式，不僅讓各校特色得以互補，也為系統內外的學生提供更廣闊的學習平臺與可能性，充分展現台聯大系統共榮共好的精神。

政大給考生的一封信：115學年度會計學系碩士班入學考試「會計學」試題釋疑

	字體大小調整
	[小](javascript:void(0);)
[中](javascript:void(0);)
[大](javascript:void(0);)

您的瀏覽器不支援JavaScript功能，若網頁功能無法正常使用時，請開啟瀏覽器JavaScript狀態

			日期 :
			 2026-03-07 

			單位 : 
			教務處綜合業務組

針對外界關注本校115學年度碩士班會計學系碩士班入學考試「會計學」部分試題與補習班模擬試題相似之爭議，本校於2月8日接獲相關訊息後，立即要求學系與命題委員針對疑義，提出說明，並於2月11日回覆陳情人。3月2日再次接獲包含更多細節之檢舉信，立即啟動專業審查機制，邀集四位具中級會計學專業背景之審查委員（包含2位校內及2位校外委員），就試題內容、命題架構及實質考點進行獨立審閱與比對分析。3月4日本校招生委員會針對四份審查意見，進行審議。經充分討論後，同意四份審查意見之評議。並決議依本校招生程序，公告面試錄取名單。以下針對審查意見之三個面向加以說明：

一、就命題取材面向：本次考試會計學第四、五兩題之命題而言，命題委員係就國家考試與教科書之習見題型，經過整合調整而為之。例如第四題其命題之構想來自國家考試105年關務特考計算題第二題與相關教科書練習題。第五題則以111年地方特考三等財稅行政選擇題第1題為基本思路之來源，題目已經過擴充與深化。上述資料均為公開資料。

二、就雷同之可能性面向：1、中級會計學係高度專業之學科，且為準則導向學科（IFRS架構）。因此不同試題之間出現部分情境或題型相似，為該學科常見現象，並非任何單一補習班所獨有。例如補習班題目經常與教科書之練習題、各大學會計學系碩士班入學考試，及國家考試之命題，出現雷同之現象。2、以本次考試之第4題為例，部分雷同點如出售半數以「公允價值」評價債券之比例設定，即為中會教科書或國家考試常見之設定。再如，考題所問每股盈餘計算至小數點後第二位，此乃財務報表編製之共通格式，我國上市櫃公司財報皆是如此。因此，許多看似相同的設定，乃是該學科考試之常見現象，不宜率然謂之有洩題情事。

三、本校命題與坊間題目之差異：經由以上之說明，可見該科命題常有相同標準設定之現象。然本校題目已經過深化，其命題點已有所不同：

第四題旨在評量考生對綜合損益表編製及其對資產負債表影響的整體掌握程度，要求考生作答的三個小題，考生必須對(1)PPE之土地採用重估價模式及後續處分，(2)FVOCI債券之評價及後續部分處分，(3)確定福利計劃之再衡量，(4)待出售停業單位之損益衡量等，這四個情況都能正確理解後，才能編製出正確的綜合損益表及計算資產負債表結果。至於補習班模擬試題各自是一個片段性知識點之測驗，與本校試題第四題是結合多種情況同時發生下的整體性知識點測驗，有所區別。

第五題考試的重點是測驗考生對於中會PPE單元相關會計處理的綜合了解程度，考題涵蓋PPE單元相關會計處理。考生作答包括五個小題：(1)PPE資產交換之損益計算，(2)PPE資產發生減損後之減損迴轉利益金額計算，(3)PPE資產重分類為待出售非流動資產當年度之損益計算，(4)PPE資產重分類為待出售非流動資產次年度實際處分之損益結果，(5)重估價模式之不動產轉列為投資性不動產之分錄。因此，補習班試題考中會PPE單元的二個片段知識，不能等同本校考題第五題測試PPE單元完整知識點的題目設計及測驗目標。綜上所述，本次命題與坊間題目存在明顯之差異。

針對外界流傳「參加補習班模考即可取得50分」的說法，經專業審查逐題比對後認為與事實存在明顯落差。題目相似處多屬文字與情境元素或題型結構上的相似，但命題之設問重視考生思維層次的辯證與整合，考試重點不同，本校試題與補習班試題自然產生明顯差異。

審查結果亦顯示，本校試題與補習班試題在命題架構及實質考點上均存在明顯差異。外部試題多屬單一知識點或單一交易情境之片段式測驗，而本校試題則採整合式題組設計，考生需整合多項會計觀念並進行分析與判斷，其評量重點與作答要求之測驗深度均明顯不同，兩者在命題本質與評量目的上並不相同。

總之，部分情境之相似並不等同於試題雷同，尤其在多重測驗目標整合之下，設問已然不同，難度自然提高，故與坊間題目有別。綜合專業審查結果，本次試題具備專業評量功能，整體命題屬合理範圍，未影響考試公平性。

本校將持續秉持嚴謹與專業原則，確保考試制度之公平與公信力，並感謝社會各界的關心與監督。同時，本校辦理各項考試業務，仍將極力維護考生的權益。

同時錄取「115學年度大學辦理特殊選才招生」多校系者。

「2026 UAiTED創新創業競賽」已於 6 月 3 日正式開放學校提名。

「2026 UAiTED創新創業競賽」已於 6 月 3 日正式開放學校提名。

			日期 :
			 2026-06-09 

			單位 : 
			台聯大-政大辦公室

【台聯大政大辦公室訊】                            

「2026 UAiTED創新創業競賽」（2026 UAiTED Innovation Competition）報名簡章與活動內容已全面上線。今年大賽以「AI for Everyday Life- AI生活創新」為核心主題，廣邀聯盟大學合組新創團隊，共同競逐總額三萬七千美元的榮譽！  

今年創新競賽主題針對Pre-A的潛力新創。即針對已完成種子基金、具備市場可行性或已有初始收入、已做好A輪融資規模擴張準備，並獲得市場接受的初步憑據（如累計30萬美元以上募資金額）的Pre-A 階段新創團隊。參賽團隊經過跨國混編，以及產業對接，同時需由UAiTED聯盟成員學校或特邀學校所推薦，且團隊中必須包含至少一名全職在學學生或學校教員所組成，人數不拘。每所成員大學最多可推薦 3 支新創團隊參賽。

本競賽旨在挖掘具備高潛力的校園新創團隊，並透過跨區域、跨文化與跨學科的交流，加強全球頂尖人才的培育與國際影響力。

競賽分為兩輪評選：

初賽：針對書面審查，參賽團隊需於7月30日（四）前提交10頁以內的英文簡報，由國際評審團針對市場需求、創新性、商業模式及可執行度來進行評分。 

總決賽：最終晉級的6支入圍團隊，將可參加於10月20日（二）在台北舉辦的總決賽。主辦單位UAiTED將全額贊助每隊最多3名成員的來回機票與住宿費用，讓學生創業家們能親臨國際舞台開拓視野。 

本次競賽的獎勵機制設有三大部分：除了金獎一萬五千美元（約合新台幣48萬元）；銀獎八千美元（約合新台幣25萬元）；銅獎四千美元（約合新台幣13萬元）的現金獎勵。

獲獎團隊還能在2027年獲得為期一年的專屬新創導師輔導（Mentorship），並獲得企業資源對接、市場洞察、企業參訪、商務網絡引薦，以及拓展海外市場的策略性支援。這對於渴望將校園創意規模化、邁向國際A輪融資的學生團隊而言，是個絕佳機會。  

UAiTED聯盟由台港星馬共17所頂尖學府組成，致力於推動校際在教育合作、產業實習、創新競賽及產學研發等面向的交流，培育具備國際視野與跨域能力的未來人才。今年也特別邀請來自日本、澳洲、泰國和越南的六所大學共同參與。

詳細的競賽規可直接email詢問，以及參閱[官網](https://uaited.ust.edu.tw/xmdoc/cont?xsmsid=0K135538085390931117&sid=0Q153373712913126466)。

【競賽核心資訊摘要】

活動主題：「AI for Everyday Life-創新日常生活的AI解決方案」

參賽資格：UAiTED成員校培育之 Pre-A 新創團隊，且至少含一名在學學生或教職員。

學校提名：6月3日（三）至7月1日（三）。

報名截止：7月5日（日）。

初賽書面資料提交截止：（需全英文準備）：7月30日（四）。

公佈決賽入圍者（入圍 6 隊）：9月4日（五）。

總決賽（在台北；詳情待公佈）：10月20日（二）。

【台聯大政大辦公室訊】                            

在資訊爆炸的時代，你知道如何運用數位資源自主學習嗎？

UAiTED（全球產學未來人才培育策略聯盟）與香港科技大學(HKUST，簡稱香港科大)合辦最新高效學習的線上課程「Learning Better in Digital Higher Education」，即將強勢登場。

這場課程特別邀請到多年深耕數位高等教育的香港科大教育創新中心主任Sean McMinn博士親自授課。McMinn博士不僅推動數位教學，更是國際知名的數位教育科技研究者，也是將數位媒體整合在高等教育的先驅。2007年他憑藉規劃設計播客（Podcast）教學，而榮獲教學創新獎，極具創新教學理念，打破傳統教育的框架。

這次由香港科大開辦的系列課程自7月29日（三）至31日（五），為期三天，將聚焦於如何聰明運用數位工具，以及培養學生在數位浪潮下掌握自我學習的核心技能。報名自6月25日（四）至7月12日（日）止，名額有限。歡迎渴望大腦升級的大學生、研究生與教學助理，不要錯過與國際大師一同翻轉學習思維！

蘇蘅系統副校長於首場課程開始前致詞，勉勵跨國學生把握線上學習機會，從不同專業角度理解AI發展與人機協作的未來趨勢。（照片來源：台聯大政大辦公室）

蔡炎龍學務長授課現場，教發中心同仁協助專業錄影與遠距教學設備操作。（照片來源：台聯大政大辦公室）

蘇蘅系統副校長於首場課程開始前致詞，勉勵跨國學生把握線上學習機會，從不同專業角度理解AI發展與人機協作的未來趨勢。（照片來源：台聯大政大辦公室）

蔡炎龍學務長授課現場，教發中心同仁協助專業錄影與遠距教學設備操作。（照片來源：台聯大政大辦公室）

王華教授與教發中心同仁於課前測試遠距教學設備，確認課程畫面、收音及互動功能。（照片來源：台聯大政大辦公室）

陳宜秀教授進行「從設計思考到人工智慧」線上課程，並回答同學提問。（照片來源：台聯大政大辦公室）

			日期 :
			 2026-06-25 

			單位 : 
			台聯大-政大辦公室

【台聯大政大辦公室訊】                            

AI快速發展，正持續改變高等教育的教學現場與學習方式。

政治大學教務處教學發展中心（以下簡稱教發中心）與UAiTED（全球未來產學人才培育策略聯盟）攜手合作，近日辦理六門AI線上先導課程，吸引跨國逾600名學生報名，累計超過1,000人次參與。

本次課程為政大參與UAiTED AI線上系列課程的首場，由六位政大教師輪番授課，結合跨域師資與線上互動教學設計，吸引聯盟17校學生踴躍參與。

為提供17校學生穩定且具互動性的線上學習體驗，教發中心運用教育學院井塘樓413（PBL）教室及相關設備，協助教師進行同步線上授課。透過即時互動、畫面切換、數位教學工具與雙向翻譯AI字幕，讓來自不同地區的師生即使隔著螢幕，也能像在同一間教室裡交流討論，讓跨國教學不再只是距離上的挑戰，而成為另一種學習的可能。

政大教師群為本次跨校課程悉心準備，於課程中展現多元學科與AI應用結合的特色。課堂除介紹AI基礎概念，也引導學生從倫理、設計思考、認知學習、AR眼鏡與商業應用等不同面向，理解AI在未來社會與專業領域中的影響。

「老師上課很活潑，內容也很容易理解。」上課過程中，學生對教師的授課方式與課堂互動留下深刻印象。

蔡炎龍教授為首場課程授課教師，曾在政大創下千人搶修課程的紀錄。本次以「從Prompt到Agent：讓AI學會你的思考方式」為題，從「AI究竟是什麼」的基本問題出發，帶領學生理解AI模型如何透過輸入與輸出進行學習，並以預測下一個詞元（token）的方式生成文字、程式碼與回應。他也介紹AI Agent如何透過反思、工具使用、規劃與多代理協作等方式，從單純回應問題，進一步發展為能協助完成任務的智慧系統。

在代理式AI與穿戴科技的應用面向上，林日璇教授以「代理式AI：AI × AR眼鏡」為題，從生成式AI、多模態AI到代理式AI的發展脈絡切入，說明AI正從螢幕中的文字互動，逐步走向結合身體、空間與環境感知的具身智慧。課程中，她介紹AI與AR智慧眼鏡如何透過語音、影像、場景理解與個人化記憶，讓使用者在真實場域中即時取得資訊與協助，並延伸討論其在工作流程、學習情境、醫療照護與日常生活中的應用。

陳宜秀教授則從設計思考切入人工智慧，帶領學生重新思考科技與人類需求之間的關係。並指出，人類運用科技改善生活的能力並非始於AI，而是源自文明發展以來持續演進的設計思維。面對AI快速發展，學生不僅需要理解技術如何解決問題，更應重新培養提出關鍵問題的能力，思考未來真正需要回應的是什麼，並以負責任的態度運用AI。

面對生成式AI逐漸成為學生常用學習工具，劉怡君教授以「從認知科學探討如何使用GenAI深度學習」為題，帶領學生從認知、後設認知與學習歷程理解AI使用的風險與可能。劉怡君指出，學習並非只是累積資訊，而是透過知識基模的建構、重組、整合與遷移，使學習者能理解核心原理並應用於不同情境。除此之外，若過度依賴AI直接完成問題，容易形成只追求答案的「手段—目的」式學習；學生應學會判讀、評估並運用AI回饋，培養後設認知與AI回饋素養。

王華教授則以「我與我的聊天機器人：與AI夥伴的倫理相遇」為題，引導學生從日常使用經驗進入AI倫理思考。課程以「我們正在與AI形成什麼關係」為核心問題，討論聊天機器人如何在工具、鏡子、陪伴者與協作者之間模糊界線。她以「從鏡子到稜鏡」的比喻說明，AI並非單純反映使用者的想法，而是會重新折射、整理並組合人的語言、情緒與期待；因此，使用者感覺被理解，並不等於真正被理解。

課程最後延伸至商管場域，曾擔任「電子支付創新實驗室」執行長的張欣綠教授於「AI在商管領域之應用」課程中，帶領學生理解AI如何改變企業競爭與價值創造模式。課程從AI的基礎概念出發，進一步探討其在行銷、財務、供應鏈管理、醫療及製造等領域的應用。她指出，AI已能協助企業提供個人化顧客體驗、提升營運效率、降低成本、分析大量資料並優化決策流程。透過企業案例與實務情境，學生得以理解企業如何運用AI重塑商業流程，並發展新的商業模式。

隨著課程圓滿落幕，學生對課程內容與互動方式反應熱烈，不僅促進不同國家學生在同一課堂中交流觀點、累積跨文化學習經驗，也進一步展現政大在跨國遠距教學及AI跨域課程設計上的教學量能。

政大場次完成後，下一場UAiTED AI系列課程將由馬來西亞拉曼大學（UTAR）接續辦理，持續推動聯盟學生跨校、跨國的AI學習交流！

【台聯大政大辦公室訊】                            

116年度「各榮民總醫院及台灣聯合大學系統合作研究計畫」（簡稱榮台聯大合作研究計畫）已自115年6月15日（一）起受理申請，至115年7月15日（三）止。本計畫係由臺北、臺中、高雄榮民總醫院及台灣聯合大學系統（中央大學、政治大學、清華大學、陽明交通大學）共同推動，期透過跨機構合作研究，提升研究教學品質並深化學術交流。

本申請案僅受理整合型研究計畫，整合型計畫須包含至少二個子計畫。計畫需由榮總與台聯大系統研究人員共同提出，惟專職於學校而於榮總兼職之醫師，應與學校研究人員合作提出計畫，且所有子計畫主持人不得均為同一機構之醫師及單位。

榮台聯大合作研究重點包括醫院管理、衛生政策、醫學倫理、基礎科學與生物醫學、生物電子、臨床醫學、醫學工程、生物資訊等跨機構、跨領域整合型研究。

本校今年5月18日已與臺北榮民總醫院共同辦理研究交流媒合會，與北榮醫生與醫療專家深度交流，促進校內教師與臨床醫師跨領域對話。

有意申請者請至「臺北榮總／榮總台灣聯大專題研究計畫管理系統」提出申請：https://rg.vghtpe.gov.tw/VGHWPR/

線上申請系統僅限各機構區段 IP 使用。研究計畫如涉及人體試驗、基因重組實驗或動物實驗者，應於申請時檢附相關委員會核准文件或送件證明。首次申請者請至「臺北榮總／榮總台灣聯大專題研究計畫管理系統」點選「帳號註冊」，完成帳號開通後即可登入系統進行計畫申請。

本年度申請通過之計畫，預計自116年1月1日起至116年12月31日止執行。

2026年度榮總台灣聯合大學系統暨研究合作成果發表會海報。（照片來源：研發處）

			日期 :
			 2026-06-11 

			單位 : 
			台聯大-政大辦公室

【台聯大政大辦公室訊】                            

台灣聯合大學系統（以下簡稱台聯大系統）與榮民總醫院體系日前共同主辦「2026年度研究合作成果發表會」，政大副校長陳樹衡在專題演講時強調，AI是否引領人類進入另一個「軸心時代」，應重新回顧歷史對人文社會科學的影響。他鼓勵在場人士思考人類如何從求生存，特別是合作與利他的「內共生」理論，反思如何共赴AI與人類更高層次的文明實現。

陳樹衡認為，AI浪潮帶來的核心議題從來不只是技術突破，而是AI作為人類創造的新物種，理應與人類共赴「自我超越」的文明實現。他肯定當前AI為人類帶來前所未有技術力量，解決物質需求。然而，也指出，真正改變文明的，是價值觀與精神層次的提升。

陳樹衡以三位對後世影響很深的醫生：坎農、羅森布魯斯及雅斯佩斯之啟發，大膽預言並強調AI與人類共存的未來課題，是人類反思「做人的意義」；認為人類是目前唯一能將意義、價值、超越等理念，發展到複雜且綿延的物種，AI是人類創造和帶有人類DNA的新物種，應承繼人類對意義與價值的追求，共同邁向更高層次的自我超越與文明實現，而非停留在技術的控制與精準。

陳樹衡的演講以「AI會迎來人類歷史上的另外一個新時代嗎？」為題，探討醫學與科學發展在AI時代的使命，鼓勵與會醫生和學者專家從人類定位和文明價值，反思未來AI文明的新挑戰，贏得現場人士熱烈迴響。

本屆「優良論文獎」首獎由中央大學生醫理工學院王健家院長及團隊獲得。另有三場成果發表會，分別由陽明交通大學黃奇英院長及團隊、清華大學王廷瑋團隊，和陽明交通大學連正章教授團隊進行分享。

中大教授王健家與研究團隊的得獎論文，解開關鍵酵素在蛋白質合成與神經退化性疾病之間的聯結，能將基因密碼精準翻譯成蛋白質。這項研究在基礎醫學上取得重大突破，協助醫學界進一步理解人類基因突變、神經退化性疾病，以及各類臨床罕見疾病的致病機轉。

王健家院長團隊與榮總體系臨床醫師跨院結盟，透過解析tRNA修飾酵素Thg1的關鍵功能，揭開神經退化疾病的新分子機制，並為小腦萎縮症、巴金森氏症等疾病開啟新的治療與藥物研發方向，深受肯定，榮獲第一名。

臺北榮民總醫院院長陳威明於開幕式致詞表示，自1987年以來，榮總與台聯大系統的合作已近四十年，樹立了台灣醫學與高等教育合作的重要典範。從最初的研究交流，到今日涵蓋基礎生物醫學、臨床醫學到智慧醫療與工程技術等領域的共同研發，展現教育與醫學攜手所開啟的更多可能。而隨著政治大學加入台聯大系統，這條合作軸線進一步延伸至人文、法律、倫理與傳播等領域，也期許未來榮台聯大計畫持續深化合作，提升臺灣醫療研究能量。

台聯大系統主席陳力俊致詞中強調，台聯大系統整合平臺的核心優勢就在「促進跨校資源共享」。陳力俊特別點出，今年政大共有4件研究成果參與發表，更有3件聚焦於人工智慧（AI）應用，顯示AI已躍升為生物醫學領域最具潛力與爆發力的研究方向。

政大校長李蔡彥亦呼應，政大作為人文社會科學重鎮，能在精準醫療浪潮中，貢獻獨特的人文與倫理視角，政大新康健計畫更結合與醫療體系持續深化目標，並致力推動健康福祉與社會永續。

陳威明這次特別準備北榮開發的「臺灣防災包」作為伴手禮。他特別介紹這個由北榮設計、以實用輕便為核心的防災包，是個附反光條、防潑水背包，內附10件套包括：乾電池行動充電器、可折疊水袋、附凝固劑的緊急衛生袋、壓縮毛巾、醫療口罩、鋁箔保暖毯、充氣枕頭與眼罩，另有關鍵時刻重要指引的「防災避難手冊」。他希望藉此提升國人具備自救及保護能力。

本次的各項合作創新成果共展出三大突破，首先是：陽明交大黃奇英院長團隊分享「胞外體核酸療法靶向治療罕見疾病的臨床病灶」研究，已在動物實驗中展現潛力。清大王廷瑋副教授團隊榮獲「未來科技獎」的「新技術型態心臟監測平臺開發」的非接觸式生物感測器，讓健康管理融入日常生活。最後，陽明交大連正章院長團隊也發表「人類癲癇顆粒細胞中的基底樹突：病理生理學、微結構與臨床相關性」的研究成果。

現場亦展示50組獲補助的研究成果海報，並參與評選，最後由12組脫穎而出，為臺灣智慧醫療永續發展注入創新火種。

【台聯大政大辦公室訊】                            

跨境電商已迎來AI全面自動化的新時代，全球產學未來人才培育策略聯盟（UAiTED）攜手國立臺灣科技大學（NTUST），將於8月24日（一）至28日（五）推出「E-Commerce Across Border」（跨境電子商務） 線上課程。報名時間自7月20日（一）至8月5日（三），不限科系。

本次課程先由兩位臺科大教師開場，分享學理及實務經驗。第一位登場的是臺科大管院專案助理教授張恩欣，她不帶學生死背課文，將教學生如何精準洞悉數位消費者的「讀心術」。多次獲得校內傑出教學獎、專精於電子商務、網路行銷、人工智慧及其應用領域的臺科大企管系欒斌教授，將使用最淺顯易懂的方式，從設計數位雙生、AI產品影片、AI代理工作流程與人機協同，深入電商的「軍火庫」，並梳理數位行銷的底層邏輯和最新演變。本課程特別邀請BENQ亞太區梁啟宏總裁（Jeffrey Liang），從國際角度檢視AI在跨境應用。梁總裁根據實戰經驗，教授國際品牌是如何在跨境電商戰場上攻城掠地，並做出具國際視野的決策，培養對市場變化的戰略思維！

由溫世仁文教基金會支持成立的UAiTED，持續透過國際頂尖大學的合作課程，將這五天淬鍊的機會，特別開放給UAiTED聯盟在學學生，希望學生精準掌握跨境電商與AI應用基礎的先備知識。全程透過五場線上講座，讓學生學習科技串連跨境電商的實際經驗。

李蔡彥上任後推動「數位賦能」與「人文AI」等發展方向，並強調以「證據為本」來推動校務。他認為，仍應保留對人的專業信任，讓人文與科技在校園中形成互補。

面對AI科技浪潮，李蔡彥認為政大應以人文強項為基礎，並透過台聯大拓展與理工及醫學領域的合作，讓不同學科之間形成互補，開展更多跨域學習與研究的可能。

李蔡彥上任後推動「數位賦能」與「人文AI」等發展方向，並強調以「證據為本」來推動校務。他認為，仍應保留對人的專業信任，讓人文與科技在校園中形成互補。

面對AI科技浪潮，李蔡彥認為政大應以人文強項為基礎，並透過台聯大拓展與理工及醫學領域的合作，讓不同學科之間形成互補，開展更多跨域學習與研究的可能。

			日期 :
			 2026-06-30 

			單位 : 
			台聯大-政大辦公室

採訪日期：2026.03.26

撰文者：姜期儒

「不是什麼事情都第一，但我們可以是唯一。」

「科技對人文的同學來講，好像是一對翅膀，他們原本就可以跑得很快了，現在可以飛起來。」

「合作不只是 Take，也要想辦法 Give。我覺得需要更大膽、勇敢地去嘗試一些新的可能。」

　　政大校長李蔡彥身上，有種不急不徐的沉著。身為政大首位資工背景的校長，他的言談保有理工訓練的條理與節制，並習慣以「證據為本」（Evidence-based）的態度來推動校務。然而，為執掌這所人文底蘊深厚大學，他同時展現了謙遜且具備深厚關懷的治理哲學，重視文化養成與長期投入的效果，「我們比較傾向於儒家的思維，就是相信人，相信人的專業判斷。」他說。

　　在政大邁向百年校慶、加入台聯大滿五周年之際，李蔡彥順利連任。他強調，在未來的任期內，他最重要的使命為建立具獨特性的政大文化，「或許不是什麼事情都第一，但是我們可以是唯一。」李蔡彥表示，當科技快速改變世界，他更關心的是，這所人文社科見長的學校，如何在既有基礎上回應新的環境挑戰。

從科技素養出發　啟動文科生的跨域可能

　　從火的發明到電力的普及，每一代技術革命都在推進人類文明，而李蔡彥認為，貫穿其中的始終是人文的精神。「人文的精神，就是在推崇人的價值，」他指出，理工訓練往往看重「物」的開發，但人文社科涵養的則是對「人」的深層理解，而兩者的互補視角，在 AI 浪潮下顯得格外關鍵。

　　李蔡彥以基因編輯為例，警示當代對科技發展失控的疑慮，「基因編輯已有明確的倫理規範，是因為我們預見了風險，AI 也可能是這樣的怪物，目前大眾多半只看到好處，卻忽略了潛藏的威脅。」他認為，具備歷史、哲學與社會學訓練的人文學者，更能預測科技對人類生存、公平性及數位落差等層面的衝擊，而這正是制定 AI 治理規範，並確保科技不偏離人性軌道的重要力量。

　　有鑑於此，李蔡彥特別重視「科技素養」，更積極推動科技教育普及化，並將其視為引發學生多元探索的奠基工作。具體而言，政大開設「AI 微學程」，協助非資訊背景的學生掌握 AI 工具，更透過舉辦「Innofest 資訊創新專題展」，鼓勵學生應用科技，將人文洞察轉化為具體的解決方案。李蔡彥在展覽中發現，政大學生的作品不同於純技術導向的提案，展現了強大的「問題洞察力」與「人文關懷」，能從不同角度看見社會痛點，「科技對人文的同學來講，好像是一對翅膀，他們原本就可以跑得很快了，現在可以飛起來。」他堅定地說。

打破單一思維　台聯大提供跨域探索機會

　　李蔡彥笑稱自己是典型的「理工男」。來到政大之前，他一直專精於理工領域，思維框架也幾乎全由理工邏輯構成，是政大這個環境，讓他開始接觸另一種理解世界的方式。李蔡彥分享了自身的跨域經驗，有次，他與政大傳播學院的陳百齡老師、吳筱玫老師合作，在一次次的對話與計畫推進的過程中，才逐漸意識到人文學者看問題的角度與自己截然不同。李蔡彥回顧道：「這過程讓我有機會了解人文社科老師在想什麼，那就讓我的思想慢慢打開了，就可以更容易去體諒，或知道某個領域發展的困難。」

　　「以我的角度來講，我需要這樣才有辦法把學校的資源做合理的配置，以及幫助不同領域去發展。」李蔡彥直言，這份理解對他的校務治理至關重要，而正因為自己曾因跨領域合作的環境受益，他希望能將同樣的機會延伸給更多人，「我既然是受惠的人，我也希望我過去有的跨域機會和環境，也可以讓其他老師、其他同學受惠。」

　　因此，李蔡彥認為，台聯大系統正扮演著製造跨域學習與合作機會的平台，與他的理念不謀而合。尤其政大雖是人文領域最完整的大專院校，但學術拼圖仍有缺口，加入台聯大後，能以相對低的行政成本，為政大師生開啟理工、醫學、藝術等領域的機會之門 ，讓政大師生得以接觸原本難以觸及的學科，對此他樂見其成。

　　具體而言，台聯大目前已提供跨校選課、轉系與輔系，也共同合作學位學程。李蔡彥提到，如傳播學院參與的「亞際文化研究國際碩士學位學程」即是四校合作的典範，讓老師與學生能直接接觸不同校風的專業。他強調，學校的責任是持續養成這種文化，讓跨領域合作不再是口號，「這個也不是一天兩天就能做起來，一定是長期的投入，有這樣的文化和環境，大家就會覺得是理所當然。」他認為，當跨域學習與合作成為日常，就具備了自然延續的力量。

積極推動遠距課程　盼擴大跨校學習機會

　　在台聯大的合作上，李蔡彥最期待深化的面向是遠距與混成學習。他坦言，許多老師對遠距教學的成效持保留態度，原因在於，若僅是把實體講座課程轉為線上影片，效果可能會從 100 分降到 80 分。但他認為，對那些受限於地理距離、原本完全沒有機會修課的學生來說，遠距教學創造的是從 0 到 80 分的價值。「有些很好的課，如果不用遠距或混成的方式上，同學也就沒有機會修。」李蔡彥重申，遠距教學真正的意義，在於讓跨校的學習機會從只是少數人的選項，變成每個學生都能觸及的資源。

　　「用單向傳授的教學方法，早晚會過時。」李蔡彥補充，在知識取得已極為容易的時代，老師在課堂上的價值，不再只是傳遞內容，而是引導學生運用各種工具去實踐想法、解決問題。他認為，課堂真正難以被取代的，是人與人之間即時的互動，包括表情、情緒與當下的來回對話，這些是目前AI仍難以複製的。遠距教學若能圍繞這個核心來設計，效果未必遜於實體課堂，他也補充，遠距教學的效果好壞，根本上取決於教學設計，而教學方式本就需要與時俱進。

　　為了讓更多老師願意嘗試，政大近年積極建置「混成教室」，盡可能降低老師在操作上的負擔，讓錄影、直播與同步教學能夠一鍵完成。「只要門檻夠低，老師去用的機會就大。」目前電算中心的講堂已率先啟用，李蔡彥也將持續朝每棟教學大學都有一間的目標推進。

從行政走向學術合作　強化校際研究動能

　　五年下來，台聯大的合作在行政層面已相當成熟。李蔡彥表示，四校在行政經驗的分享上「是蠻常態化的」，他認為，接下來值得更積極推動的，是老師之間的研究合作。他觀察到，老師之間往往缺乏一個能認識彼此的場合，研究合作的啟動多半靠老師各自的人脈網絡。

　　對此，除了舉辦學生的社團交流與運動會外，師長的交流活動也可納入考量。李蔡彥也建議，若能在台聯大系統層級設立「研究種子基金」，支持跨校、跨領域的老師共同提案研究計畫，也將有助於整合各校領域強項，深化研究合作。

　　李蔡彥也談到政大近年提出的「顯學計畫」。過去政大各學院的研究較為分散，各自獨立發展，顯學計畫的目的，即在於找出具潛力的跨領域議題，整合不同學院的資源，讓研究成果更具整體能見度。例如，「新康健社會」是政大近年關注的議題，雖政大在生物技術上並非強項，但可以從心理學、政策與傳播等社會科學視角切入，補足理工院校較缺乏的人文觀點。他期待，台聯大三校在理工與醫學上的積累，能與政大的社科視角互補，「我們也可以去加入他們的關注的議題，雙向合作都很好。」

四校關係如手足　互惠與共享為合作基礎

　　採訪最後，李蔡彥談起他對台聯大四校關係的理解，「我們跟國外的合作學校叫姊妹校，是夥伴的關係，那我覺得跟台聯大另外三個學校的關係，應該比夥伴更進一步，我們應該都是在一個家庭裡面的兄弟姐妹。」他補充，兄弟姊妹之間有各自的個性，也存在良性競爭，但根本上是希望彼此都好的深厚情誼。

　　「合作不只是 Take，更要思考如何 Give。」展望未來，李蔡彥期待能持續突破既有框架，在互惠的基礎上嘗試更多新的合作可能，而政大作為台聯大中獨特的人文角色，也將持續為台聯大注入不同的觀點與動能。

受訪者基本資料： 

國立政治大學第15任校⾧，曾任教育部資訊及科技教育司司⾧、政大創新與創造力研究中心主任、人文創新數位學院執行⾧等職。畢業於國立臺灣大學農業機械工程學系，並取得美國史丹佛大學資訊科學碩士、機械工程博士學位，專⾧領域為人工智慧、資料分析與資訊科學教育。2022年首度就任政大校⾧，並於2026年順利連任，為政大首位資訊科學背景出身的校⾧，任內致力推動科技素養教育及「人文AI」計畫，探索人文價值與科技發展的共存之道。

「大學系統當時在台灣是首創，一切從零開始，可以說是篳路藍縷啊。」陳正成回憶道，評估小組的工作並不輕鬆，需要對四校的教學、研究、行政等合作進行全面評估，也必須撰寫計劃、報請教育部批准，一來一回非常具有挑戰性。

「大學系統當時在台灣是首創，一切從零開始，可以說是篳路藍縷啊。」陳正成回憶道，評估小組的工作並不輕鬆，需要對四校的教學、研究、行政等合作進行全面評估，也必須撰寫計劃、報請教育部批准，一來一回非常具有挑戰性。

			日期 :
			 2026-06-28 

			單位 : 
			台聯大-政大辦公室

採訪日期：2024.06.18

撰文者：姜期儒

　　於台灣聯合大學服務18年的陳正成教授，現任國立陽明交通大學熱帶醫學科兼任教授，是台灣聯大的重要推手。從草創到執行，陳正成曾擔任系統副主席，直到去年底仍以顧問身分協助推動四校聯合計劃，並編撰《台灣聯合大學系統二十年》一書，為台灣聯大的發展帶來重大貢獻。回顧推動台灣聯大的心路歷程，陳正成以「篳路藍縷」來形容，途中儘管困難重重，他始終堅信大學系統有望打破僵化的教育體制，並以學生的利益與教育出發，為台灣高教注入新氣象。

與台灣聯大的18年淵源

　　台灣聯大的成立源於2002年教育部推動的「推動研究型大學整合計畫」，當時，國立陽明大學、國立交通大學、國立清華大學和國立中央大學四校認為，彼此理念相近且在多個研究領域可以互補，並由四校副校長、教務長和研發長組成評估小組，負責評估組建大學系統的可行性。時任國立陽明大學教務長的陳正成教授，在因緣際會下成為台灣聯大評估小組的主要成員之一，至此展開在台灣聯大長達18年的服務生涯。

　　光是推動「大學系統」取得合法地位，前後就花了六年。不管是法規問題還是內部溝通問題，陳正成全程參與，「畢竟大學系統在台灣是新創的，所以一定要有耐心、慢慢做。認為好的方向就要往前走，慢慢去推動。」

跨校合作的價值體現

　　陳正成認為，台灣高等教育僵化，可能導致研究發展的限制，學生更缺乏彈性選擇與適性探索的空間。因此，他期待台灣聯大的構想逐步打破傳統的學校及科系藩籬，為學生提供更多元、更優質的學習資源。其中，陳正成最印象深刻的創舉為「跨校轉系所」。多年前，一位曾考上醫學放射系的同學便受益於這項政策，充分體現跨校合作的價值。

　　陳正成分享，這位同學在進入陽明大學後，才發現自己並不適合醫學領域。同學對放射線及醫學影像感到恐懼，尤其實驗室裡擺放著許多醫學儀器，她不但無法專心學習，也對進入實驗室感到不安。陳正成了解情況後，建議她透過台灣聯大的跨校轉系所的申請機會，嘗試到交大資財系學習。值得慶幸的是，同學展現對經濟和商業的天分與興趣，迅速適應新的學習環境，並在畢業後進入金融業工作。

　　事實上，教育部曾認為跨校轉系所的措施違反《學籍法》，一度禁止實施。然而，陳正成花了三年與教育部溝通，除了明訂僅能以生涯規劃、志趣不合為由轉學外，也確保不會打亂招生秩序。溝通過程雖然困難，但陳正成觀察到學生在求學過程中的迷茫，尤其陽明大學僅有醫學相關領域，校內轉系仍有侷限，因此他相信，這項措施可能改變學生的人生。

　　多年來時有艱辛，但「使命感」始終支撐著陳正成，他說：「畢竟當初是我們共同設計出來，那我們自己要讓它實現嘛，所以一直往下走。」

　　此外，台灣聯大的重要專案還包含「學術倫理線上課程」，這套由台灣聯大取得捐款、策劃教材，交大技術研發團隊設計的數位課程，現已推行至全國大專院校，而陳正成即是背後的主要推手。他笑著自嘲全國研究生「深受其害」，但陳正成仍自信地說：「學術倫理課程也是台灣聯大對整個高教系統帶來的重大助益，目前可能已經有超過一百萬人修習。」

踏實堅毅的工作態度

　　作為台灣聯大的創始元老及關鍵推手，陳正成見證了台灣聯大從無到有的歷程，也為台灣聯大的未來擘劃了藍圖。陳正成提到，編撰《台灣聯合大學系統二十年》專書的過程，不僅是會議與計劃資料的整理，這項工作也記錄了他的親身經歷，讓他十分感動。

　　陳正成穩健地做事態度，深受兩位前輩的影響──已故的蚊子博士連日清教授、成功防治金門血絲蟲的范秉真教授。連日清教授是同樣專長蚊子研究的陳正成的啟蒙導師，陳正成景仰與學習連日清教授嚴謹、踏實的研究風格，以及他一一採集、鑑定出台灣130種蚊子的執著精神。在的研究生涯中，連日清教授深深影響了他。

　　另外，陳正成也分享跟隨范秉真教授前往金門進行血絲蟲防治的日子。當時金門正處於戒嚴期間，雙方炮戰頻繁，夜晚更有水鬼和軍事行動的威脅，但這些並沒有阻止他們的研究工作。「有很多危險，但是范教授就是堅持要做研究，要努力去做，要去採集，一定要出去！」隨後，陳正成在炮火下進行採血工作，並以此為基礎完成碩士論文，他笑道：「啊！還好，在那好多年了，都沒有被炮彈打到。」

　　這段經歷不僅鍛煉了陳正成的研究能力，也使他堅信，無論面對多大的困難，只要堅持努力，就能夠克服困境。如同陳正成在推動跨校轉系所時，面對強硬的教育部法規限制，他仍以「為學生好」的核心理念為根基，甘願花上多年提出可行方案與促進修法。這樣的工作態度，充分體現了他對教育的熱情與服務精神，也為台灣聯大的持續發展奠定了堅實的基礎。

對台灣聯大的期許與展望

　　談及對台灣聯大的期許。陳正成強調「跨領域人才」的重要性，這也正是台灣聯大的核心精神之一。他指出：「大學是創造知識的地方，不能僵化，要走在時代的尖端。」雖然台灣聯大礙於資金和法規上的限制，但仍必須嘗試突破現有框架。尤其在政大加入台灣聯大後，更加補足了原先四校在人文社會領域的缺口，陳正成樂見其成，更期待政大加入後，能使得台灣聯大更具競爭力。

　　舉例而言，中央、清大、陽交大三校近年投入於AI和半導體學院的發展，政大在此趨勢下至關重要。陳教授提醒，科技進步之快，尤其是AI的發展，不應一昧追求先進技術的研發，更需要與人文社會的融合，推動人文社會導向的AI。陳正成說：「AI單獨發展不一定對人類是最佳利益，最重要的不外乎人性。政大應該想辦法主動提出合作，將人文社會融合到AI的發展上，我個人覺得這是應該是要做的。」

　　最後，陳教授也期望大學系統能法人化，以更靈活的方式推動教育創新和發展。他相信，台灣聯大可以在未來的教育改革中繼續發揮重要作用，培養出更多跨領域的優秀人才。

台灣聯合大學系統總校長陳力俊在任內面對高教資源緊縮與制度限制，持續推動四校整合與合作。他強調，在現實條件下應「做可以做的事」，讓各校在共享資源與跨域交流中逐步凝聚，朝「四校如一校」的目標前進。

台灣聯合大學系統總校長陳力俊在任內面對高教資源緊縮與制度限制，持續推動四校整合與合作。他強調，在現實條件下應「做可以做的事」，讓各校在共享資源與跨域交流中逐步凝聚，朝「四校如一校」的目標前進。

			日期 :
			 2026-07-01 

			單位 : 
			台聯大-政大辦公室

採訪日期：2026.03.19

撰文者：姜期儒

「做可以做的事！只要每個學校都感受到益處，合作就會自然發生。」

「台聯大做的事情，就是四校都會感受到它有益處的事情。」

「希望大家更有凝聚力，這需要時間，讓大家慢慢感受到合作的好處。」

　　自 2020 年接掌台聯大系統總校長，陳力俊已帶領這個橫跨三座城市、連結近六萬名師生的學術共同體，走過了五個年頭。從清大工學院院長、清大校長，再到國科會副主委，這一路橫跨研究、行政與政策的深厚歷練，卻似乎絲毫未讓陳力俊陷入資深學者的保守框架。

　　一入座，陳力俊便談起生成式 AI，他不僅定期發表 AI 應用演講，更用它打磨投書文稿、將旅遊照片轉化為動態影片。談到興頭上，他眼神中閃爍的，依然是研究者對新事物的銳利好奇。面對 AI 浪潮接踵而來，陳力俊正以務實而前瞻的意志，在資源有限的現實中，擘畫台灣四所頂尖大學攜手合作的可能格局。

追求共好　只做「能讓四校受益」的事

　　二十多年前，台灣聯合大學系統在教育部「推動研究型大學整合計畫」的支持下成立，肩負著打造國際頂尖大學系統、與台大產生良性競爭關係的期待。陳力俊一路參與台聯大發展至今，見證了從政策鼎力支持，轉向僅靠四校共同基金運作的轉變。「你沒有經費支援，當然能做的事就少很多。」他回憶，台聯大作為全台第一個大學系統，曾坐擁十多個研究中心，如今僅存兩個，盛景不再。

　　在教育部無提供經費，且持續監督的條件下，陳力俊在連任總校長之際，悟出一套以「凝聚與共好」為核心的領導心法。「只要每個學校都覺得對自己有好處，這件事就會自動運作起來。」陳力俊坦言，他深知「四校合一」已幾乎是難以實現的目標，但他依然追求「四校如一校」的體驗。例如，跨校選課與轉學機制，可讓學生能在校園間自由探索；圖書資源的全面開放，則讓各校館藏發揮更大影響力。這些措施不需大幅改動制度，卻建立了整合的基礎。「我們一天有六班校際專車往返，今天預約他校圖書，過幾天就能拿到，」陳力俊說，「這點我們就做得很好。」

　　陳力俊總結道：「做可以做的事！」這套看似佛系的領導風格，背後其實有一條清晰的判準：凡事若能讓四校同時受益便優先推動，無法達成共識則不強求。他也直言，教育部應建立更精準的評鑑制度，並提供重點支持，否則任何具前瞻性的整合方案，終將難以為繼。

台聯大辦羅家倫學術研討會　傳揚四校教育人文理念

　　當實質資源受限，台聯大四校還能一起做些什麼？陳力俊將重點擺在深化連結，並轉而挖掘四校共有的精神資產。他認為，大學系統的合作，不應止於行政庶務，更可以來自歷史文化血脈的共鳴。而羅家倫先生，便成了他心中最完美的「台聯大精神資產」。

　　羅家倫為一名具影響力的教育家，擔任過清華大學、中央大學與政治大學校長，也曾在陽明交通大兼課，與台聯大四校皆有深厚淵源。陳力俊笑說：「我們四校，這下可能真是天作之合了！」2025年五月，陳力俊親自主導推動「鑑察世道．興國育才──羅家倫先生學術研討會」，邀請四校學者共同發表研究，讓這位同時影響四校的教育家，首次被放入台聯大的整體脈絡中重新理解，並由四校共同討論。

　　回憶起籌備過程，陳力俊分享了一段猶如「校園尋寶」般的插曲。當時，一位退休的校務人員提供了關鍵線索，指出清大校內某處，似乎有一扇羅家倫先生親筆題字的屏風。於是，團隊循線查閱圖書館的資訊系統，一路追蹤至大禮堂的貴賓室，才發現羅家倫先生的墨寶。陳力俊回憶，總務處當時特別指派了七名工作人員，慎重地合力搬運，他笑道：「看到七個人在那裡搬那幾幅大字，的確是很有趣。」

　　學術研討會結束後，政大也接棒，於達賢圖書館推出「羅家倫特展」，展出珍貴文獻與史料，讓羅家倫的思想與教育實踐有更具體的呈現。陳力俊表示，策展極耗心力，未來若能將既有展覽擴大辦理，在四校間巡迴展出，將有助於提升整體效益。他也期待能持續推動跨校文化合作，讓四校逐步累積更緊密的連結。

跨校選課行之有年　四校地理距離仍須突破

　　陳力俊認為，台聯大最具代表性的成果，莫過於行之有年的跨校選課與轉學機制。然而，在四校地理距離的先天限制下，他並不以此自滿。「雖然課程、圖書資源能夠流通，但人的移動依舊辛苦。」陳力俊指出，無論是教師跨校開課或學生奔波修課，「學分在哪裡，人就得辛苦到哪裡」的狀況，始終是整合的阻力。

　　事實上，台聯大十多年前已有「共同開放式課程 」的成功經驗，現在也有少部分課程嘗試遠距授課，這讓課程資源不再受限於專車時刻表，而是在雲端實現共享。對於持續發展遠距課程，陳力俊樂見其成，並且認為「善用科技」已是時勢所趨。然而他也直言：「部分老師對 AI 的接受度，甚至還不如學生。」由於許多老師學有專精、教材也早已準備齊全，在沒有感受到迫切需要或領受 AI 強大之處前，往往不覺得有改變的必要。

　　「如果你是一個負責人，你必須以身作則，否則你的同仁不會認真去推動。」陳力俊雖謙稱自己目前沒教課，也不是公司的負責人，但他已在日常工作中善用科技工具。例如，他會請 AI 幫忙審閱專欄稿件，也會運用 AI 製作演講簡報與插圖，並在汶萊旅遊時，嘗試將照片轉換成有趣影片。陳力俊表示，唯有讓大家看到「當你不用 AI，就會比人家差一截」的實質差距，才能推動整個大學系統進步。

「熱心生力軍」加入五周年　助人文理工跨域合作

　　談到政大加入台聯大這五年，陳力俊將政大形容為「熱心的生力軍」。「政大的積極與認真，確實提升了台聯大的精采度。」陳力俊認為，政大在人文社科領域的強項，為原本理工色彩濃厚的台聯大注入了一劑強心針。他特別提到，政大遍布海外的廣大校友網絡，更為台聯大的國際招生帶來了實質的助力，對此他也表示感謝。

　　陳力俊指出，政大的加入不只是為台聯大拓展招生、學生跨領域學習的機會，更從根本上改變了台聯大的格局。舉例而言，近年台聯大和新北市合作「共創學習計畫」，把四校的特色課程帶到高中，政大加入後，便新增了「傳播與 AI」等課程，豐富社會思辨的視角，也讓人才培育的維度變得更加完整。

　　尤其陳力俊認為，台灣的科技硬體實力堅強，但要「如何應用」新興科技，卻仍有進步的空間。而他也信手拈來，舉出多個AI深偽影像引發社會混亂的案例，以及近期爆紅的AI代理人「龍蝦（OpenClaw）」的資安疑慮，警示若忽視人類的判斷與價值考量，極可能帶來嚴重後果。對此，陳力俊提到，台聯大的角色不僅是研究「如何應用」，更要帶頭追問「如何正確地應用」。這份對AI倫理的重視，也是他認為台聯大在此時代中，最不可迴避的社會責任。

「四校如一校」　務實推進的整合願景

　　展望台聯大的未來，陳力俊依然堅定地看向「四校如一校」的整合目標。他深信，只要各校能看見彼此的優勢、分享正能量，這份整合的意志便能跨越行政藩籬，讓台聯大的學生在雲端與實體校園中，都能獲得最頂尖的競爭力。面對 AI 對高等教育的影響，陳力俊強調，領導者必須「以身作則」帶動轉型，他期待四校在各展專長的基礎上，保持追求卓越的共識，即便在經費受限的挑戰下，依然能整合成一個兼具科技實力與人文倫理關懷的頂尖大學系統。

受訪者基本資料：

現任臺灣聯合大學系統總校長，為中央研究院院士、美國材料研究學會（MRS）院士，曾任國立清華大學校長、工學院院長，並曾獲總統科學獎及教育部國家講座等學術殊榮。畢業於國立臺灣大學物理學系，並於美國柏克萊加州大學（UC Berkeley）取得物理學博士學位，為材料科學、奈米材料、電子顯微鏡等領域的物理學家。2021年就任台聯大系統總校長，並於2025年獲得四校校長共識續任，持續帶領系統邁向「四校如一校」的發展願景。
